human_substantive_critiques.issue: Lack of formal statistical variance partitioning and pairwise comparisons quantifying inter-laboratory versus treatment variation across root microbiome and exometabolome profiles.
Apparent discrepancy between root inoculum (22 PCR cycles) and media inoculum (30 PCR cycles) 16S profiles, and unexplained 'Unknown' sequence reads.
Non-standardized root image segmentation across participating laboratories (automated RhizoNet in Labs B-E versus manual ImageJ/SmartRoot in Lab A due to condensation).
Lack of a single-strain Paraburkholderia sp. OAS925 inoculation control and over-reliance on soft-agar motility to explain dominant root colonization.

ai_only_critical_catches: Unblocked pooling in Figure 2b plant shoot biomass one-way ANOVA: pooling 5 labs x 7 replicates = 35 observations per group while reporting 'n = 7' in the caption without modeling Laboratory as a fixed blocking or random effect despite major inter-lab chamber light (110 vs 150 umol/m2/s) and temperature differences.

Compositional closure artifact in Section 2.6: applying standard Gaussian two-way ANOVA directly to untransformed 16S relative abundances across treatments where Paraburkholderia sp. OAS925 accounts for ~98% of reads in SynCom17 and 0% in SynCom16 mathematically forces opposite treatment effects on all remaining taxa.

Internal discrepancy between Figure 2c caption (stating Lab A root segmentation used 'ImageJ') and Methods Section 4.3 (stating Lab A used 'SmartRoot V4.21'), plus a typographical error ('2 x 00 indexed run recipe') in Section 4.6.

records.authors: Fonseca-Garcia C, Pettinga D, Caddell D, Ploemacher H, Louie K, Bowen BP, Park J, Sanchez J, Zimic-Sheen A, Traxler MF, Northen TR, Coleman-Derr D.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Drastic difference in taxonomic composition between PacBio full-length 16S and Illumina V3-V4 16S amplicon sequencing (~1% vs. ~30% Actinobacteria in watered control roots) requiring primer-bias validation.
Overstatement in claiming that the lack of correlation between single-strain gnotobiotic drought enrichment (DE) and seedling biomass challenges the ecological 'cry for help' framework.
Lack of direct correlation analysis linking untargeted LC-MS/MS exometabolomic molecules to DE or plant growth promotion scores across the strain panel.
Need for expanded description of the genomic neighborhoods surrounding the 8 fabG and proP gene clusters and discussion of plant physiological drought responses beyond biomass.

ai_only_critical_catches: Scale-dependent ad hoc PGLS filtering across 7,737 ortholog gene clusters using raw unstandardized regression slopes and standard errors (slope > 0.25 and SE < 0.25) instead of scale-invariant t-statistics (t = slope / SE) and genome-wide Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q-values, which biases discovery toward high-copy-number gene families with large variance (such as fabG, 6-21 copies) and omits raw/adjusted p-values for the 8 candidate gene families.

Internal discrepancy in the ortholog pre-filtering variance threshold between the Results text (Line 231, stating variance < 0.2 across the 24 genomes was excluded) and the Methods text (Line 508, stating variance < 0.25 was excluded).

Pseudoreplication in the gnotobiotic sorghum seedling mono-association growth assays: treating n=15 individual seedlings pooled across 3 sealed microboxes (5 seedlings sharing root space and inoculum per box) as independent biological replicates in one-way ANOVAs and Dunnett's tests rather than treating the microbox (n=3) as the experimental unit or fitting a mixed model with (1 | box).

Arbitrary constant zero-imputation (0.0001) for undetected negative-control qPCR values and multiplication of all 5 biological replicates within a treatment group by a single group-averaged qPCR copy number prior to running two-sided t-tests for the strain DE scores.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Need for an explicit mathematical model of plasmid competition to generalize the parameter regimes under which horizontal and vertical transmission advantages allow streamlined plasmids to displace wild-type AMR plasmids.
Investigation of the faint ~1 kb deletion band in ancestral R1 colony PCR to distinguish pre-existing in vivo deletion variants from in vitro PCR template-switching across IS1 repeats.

Verification that plasmid segregation loss is negligible over 8 days so vertical competition is not confounded by plasmid-free cells, and inclusion of a full-length R1 TcR control in the barrier invasion assay.

Contextualization with prior literature on satellite plasmids (Zhang et al., 2019) and plasmid acquisition cost (Ahmad et al., 2023), and replacing 'stealth/deleted plasmids' terminology with 'streamlined plasmids'.

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematical discrepancy between the text description of the ODE model and the displayed ODE system (Methods lines 46-75): the text states that conjugation into a co-infected cell (N_WM) displaces the resident plasmid with probability 1/2 to preserve structural neutrality (citing Lipsitch et al. [59]), but the displayed equations for dN_W/dt, dN_M/dt, and dN_WM/dt omit all co-infection displacement terms (+/- 0.5*(1-k)*N_WM*lambda_i), violating structural neutrality in the printed equations (and omitting the definition of total cell density T = N_0 + N_W + N_M + N_WM).

Pseudoreplication in the exponential growth-rate statistical analysis (lm(growth_rate ~ strain * plasmid * rep_nb) with df = 518 and TukeyHSD), which treats 12 technical replicate wells on the same 96-well plate as independent error degrees of freedom rather than modeling the n = 3 independent biological cultures per strain as random effects.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Non-independence of f4 tests, absence of a domestication bottleneck in the rangewide mushi demographic inference, and question of whether fixed nonsynonymous differences in the MK test are shared ancestral fixations.
High false-positive and false-negative rates in RAiSD composite sweep scans and confounding by shared ancestral sweeps between closely related populations.
Application of rdmc to wide genomic sweep windows, bimodal standing-variation ages, and migration rate differences between maize and teosinte.

ai_only_critical_catches: Algebraic error in the false-positive-adjusted hypergeometric sweep overlap test (Materials and Methods, lines 108-122): the authors define P as the false positive rate (~0.265 from Palmar Chico subsampling), but multiply N, n1, n2, and x by P instead of precision (1 - P), and scale all four hypergeometric parameters by the same factor, which fails to model independent false-positive sweep calls across population pairs.

In-sample hyperparameter optimization bias: tuning RAiSD window size (24 SNPs), outlier cutoff, and merging distance on Palmar Chico to maximize split-sample replicate concordance and applying that single error estimate across bottlenecked teosinte populations.

Typesetting/production corruptions in the published text: three command-line/filter equations in Materials and Methods (lines 26, 58, and 90) are completely blank/omitted after colons, and line 15 contains a citation manager auto-replacement glitch ('three lanes of Haines et al., 2000, rapid run' instead of 'Illumina HiSeq 2000 rapid run').

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Need to directly test whether the embryo itself (prior to E12.5 fetal liver formation) possesses any HAAO enzymatic activity by assaying whole E11.5 embryos and E14.5 liver-excised embryos.
Lack of direct spatial/histological validation (in situ hybridization or immunohistochemistry) of scRNA-seq kynurenine pathway gene expression in the yolk sac endoderm.
Distinction between de novo NAD synthesis starting from L-tryptophan (requiring Tdo2, which is absent in mouse yolk sac endoderm) versus from maternal L-kynurenine.
Vague malformation terminology in Table S4 and need for clearer discussion of differential organ susceptibility to NAD deficiency.

ai_only_critical_catches: Analyzing the 2x2 factorial experimental design (Diet NW15 vs. NW3.5 x Genotype Haao+/- vs. Haao-/-, nested within maternal litters) at E10.5 using a 4-group one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post-hoc test instead of a two-way linear mixed-effects model accounting for the Diet x Genotype interaction and litter-level random effects.

Measurement-error and sample-unit mismatch in the E10.5 correlation analyses (Fig 5I-K) caused by pairing pooled yolk sac metabolite measurements (2-3 yolk sacs per pool) against individual embryo NAD+ measurements.

Bioinformatics reference/annotation mismatch in Methods Line 107 stating that human bulk RNA-seq reads were aligned to human reference genome hg38 but quantified against the mouse GENCODE vM10 annotation.

Deviations from the OSF preregistration (pooling pilot and main datasets for exploratory analyses, power calculation details) required explicit disclosure.

ai_only_critical_catches: Non-independence in the GLMM specification: fitting three separate binary mixed-effects logistic regressions (logit P(choice = X), Y, Z) to mutually exclusive bandit arms on the same trials and pooling their fixed-effect slopes/SEs via inverse-variance weighting treats negatively correlated multinomial outcomes as independent and underestimates standard errors by ~sqrt(3).

Typographical error in the dependent variable definition of Equation (1) in Methods, which states 'coded as 1 if the partner's choice was X on trial t' instead of 'coded as 1 if the participant's choice was X on trial t'.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Strengthen evidence that sTOs are purely fetal-derived trophoblasts without maternal epithelial or fetal stromal contamination, clarify marker selection in the bulk RNA-seq heatmap, and include uterine gland markers

Justify sTO scRNA-seq clustering resolution (5 clusters), address leaky marker expression across clusters, and explain why sTO Cluster 2 failed to map to Visium trophoblasts while Clusters 1 and 3 both mapped to Areola-2
Separate the in vivo Visium maternal-fetal CellChat signaling analysis from the sTO vs. Visium inter-trophoblast CellChat comparison

Make raw sequencing datasets and analysis code publicly available, specify multiple-testing adjusted p-value thresholds, and clarify Seurat SCT/RNA assay usage and pig-human ortholog mapping in CellChat
Questioned whether the Slingshot differentiation trajectory is truly linear (ProfTroph -> IntTroph -> Areola-2) rather than bifurcating

ai_only_critical_catches: Statistical variance compression from running differential expression (FindAllMarkers) and CellChat ligand-receptor overexpression tests on ALRA zero-imputed expression matrices (RunALRA) rather than non-imputed RNA/SCT counts.

Misattribution of sTO Cluster 4 as 'Areola-1' based on 20 shared markers dominated by mitochondrially encoded oxidative phosphorylation transcripts (COX1, COX3, ND4, CYTB), which in droplet scRNA-seq (especially as dead-cell removal was omitted for line STO02) reflects stressed/high-mitochondrial cells rather than canonical Areola-1 markers (SPINK4, CCDC162, LIF).

Internal Methods inconsistencies: gestation day reported as GD66 in Fig 3A caption vs. GD65 in Methods Line 46; contradictory sow/gilt numbers and Lutalyse induction assignments in Methods Line 41 (2 sows + 1 gilt = 3 vs. 2 gilts + 3 sows = 5); and a 1,000x volume unit typo on Line 62 ('resuspended in 500 mL of prewarmed TOM' instead of 500 uL).

Unresolved numerical discrepancies between main text and Methods in simulation specifications: (a) Main text line 157 states 40% null / 60% non-null variants, whereas Methods line 310 specifies 60% null / 40% non-null and a mean shift ratio of -0.15 / -0.125 = 1.2x alongside an SD ratio of 1.4x; (b) Main text line 183 and Figure 5 caption state 1.4x environmental amplification in the PGS simulation, whereas the generative covariance matrix in Methods line 345 uses 1.5 * sigma (1.5x amplification).

records.title: Human genetic evidence enriched for side effects of approved drugs.
records.authors: Minikel EV, Nelson MR.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: SIDER is restricted to post-marketing package inserts of approved drugs (last updated in 2015), introducing survivorship and risk-benefit bias that limits direct generalizability to preclinical/clinical-stage drug discovery safety attrition.
Potential confounding by genetic support for the drug's primary indication, target pleiotropy (number of associated genetic traits), and sensitivity to the MeSH semantic similarity threshold.
Lack of direction-of-effect concordance analysis (agonist vs. antagonist pharmacology relative to gain/loss-of-function human genetics) and breakdown by drug modality.

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe statistical non-independence in all 2x2 Fisher's exact tests and binomial logistic regressions across the 1,187,298 drug-SE pairs: treating shared-target drug pairs (567 drugs mapped to only 275 target genes, e.g., 40 drugs sharing just 7 target genes for tachycardia) and ontologically correlated MeSH SE terms as independent Bernoulli trials, massively deflating p-values (e.g., P = 7.1e-93).

Methodological contradiction between the Results text (stating drug-SE pairs with Sim(Indication, SE) >= 0.9 were removed from the analysis universe) and the Methods text (stating Sim(Genetic Trait, Indication) < 0.9 was required for a target-indication-SE trio to count as having genetic support, leaving the pair in the non-genetically-supported denominator).
Case-only conditioning (Y = 1) in the SIDER side-effect frequency and placebo-status logistic regression models (glm(sim_assoc ~ frequency)).

Unreplaced template placeholder 'X' in Supporting Information S2 Fig caption ('driven by GWAS associations for X genes: CYP19A1..., ESR1..., FGFR2..., INSR..., and SRD5A2...') and unformatted dangling reference numbers '34,35' in Methods Line 108 where the reference list ends at [26].

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Mendelian inheritance expectations for presence-absence variation (PAV) genes and potential structural/recombination mechanisms driving deviations from Mendelian ratios in F1 progeny needed formal explanation.

Genomic context and transposable element enrichment flanking PAV loci, as well as evolutionary mechanisms generating PAVs (tandem duplication, horizontal viral integration), required analysis and discussion.

Two reference gonad samples in Branchiostoma belcheri skewed the coverage-vs.-dispensable-gene correlation in Fig 1b, and BelcheriHV-1 SNP frequency/read-depth plots (Fig 3b-d) needed clearer biological explanation.
Bioinformatics pipeline and figure-generation scripts were not deposited in a public code repository.

ai_only_critical_catches: Systematic downward bias in observed F1 offspring gene absence rates relative to Mendelian expectations (39.6% vs. 50% for Class II; 17.7% vs. 25% for Class III) and 32.8% 'undetermined' parental genes caused by allowing multi-mapping reads in bwa mem combined with low (~7x) F1 sequencing depth.

Multiple internal numerical and species-label contradictions between text and tables: BelcheriHV-1 coding density reported as 72.7% in text vs. 70.4% in Table 2 (and genomic sub-blocks summing to 142.5 kb vs. 149.9 kb total length); BelcheriHV-2 ORF count reported as 72 in text vs. 74 in Table 2; big defensin absence rate reported as 77% in Results vs. 88% in Discussion; Class III F1 absence rate reported as 19% in text vs. 17.7% in Table 3; Discussion line 188 misattributing the B. floridae parent-offspring cross to B. belcheri; Fig 8 caption citing Table 2 instead of Table 3.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Test robustness of bat rsIFITM antiviral restriction across multiple MOIs, multi-cycle infection kinetics, and plasmid dosages, and compare transfected transcript levels to endogenous poly(I:C)-stimulated RsKT.01 cells
Demonstrate endogenous protein expression of both rsIFITMa and rsIFITMb isoforms in native RsKT.01 bat cells and perform loss-of-function/knockout validation
Increase sample size of cells imaged for confocal surface FLAG quantification (originally only 3 cells) and add quantitative JACoP colocalization with endosomal marker CD63
Evaluate SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (Wuhan, Delta, Omicron) and test negative imprinting of progeny virions
Discrepancy between transient transfection (Fig 3B, where rsIFITMb modestly restricts IAV) and stable transduction (S5B-C Fig, where rsIFITMb shows no restriction of IAV)
Lack of a live/dead viability dye in flow cytometry gating (S4 and S6 Figs) and request to deposit custom comparative genomics code on GitHub

ai_only_critical_catches: Annotation depth and genome assembly quality confounding in the 206-mammal RefSeq comparative splicing analysis (Fig 7D-E): species with higher-contiguity assemblies and deeper multi-tissue RNA-seq annotation simultaneously have more resolved IFITM paralogs (duplication) and more annotated splice isoforms, confounding the 2x2 Fisher's exact test positive association

Cell-level and field-level pseudoreplication in confocal microscopy statistics: treating >=30 individual cells (Fig 4B-C) or 10 fields of view (Fig 5A-B) as independent observations in unpaired t-tests without biological batch blocking or multi-group ANOVA correction

Missing public repository accession (NCBI SRA / GEO) for the primary poly(I:C)-stimulated R. sinicus RsKT.01 RNA-seq dataset generated in Fig 1B-D, plus omission of the transcript/isoform quantifier used downstream of STAR and use of unadjusted nominal p < 0.05 in edgeR

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Discrepancy between pseudovirus and live SARS-CoV-2 infection assays in LGMN-overexpressing cells due to CMV promoter silencing in the pLX304 lentiviral vector.
Clarify the cellular localization and proteolytic mechanism of LGMN (whether it compensates for TMPRSS2 or acts endolysosomally alongside CTSL) using catalytic and signal-peptide mutants.
Show data for the 3 individual sgRNAs per gene separately rather than only pooling all 3 sgRNAs into a single group in knockout validation figures.
Justify criteria for selecting top screen hits (LGMN, KCNA6) and compare screen results against previously published genome-wide SARS-CoV-2 CRISPRa screens.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Unclear diagnostic sensitivity/specificity, Ct 39 cutoff rationale, and caveat that the H5 RT-qPCR standard curve used synthetic dsDNA rather than viral RNA

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematical impossibility in reported sequencing depths (Results, line 140): the authors report an 'overall average sequencing depth of 8,176x across all samples (varying from 325x to 29,256x)', yet two sentences later state that the lowest segment average depth across all samples was 199x (NA) and the highest segment average depth was 419x (PB1)—mathematically, the overall mean across segments cannot be 8,176x (>20-fold higher than the maximum segment mean of 419x)

Sample-size / p-value impossibility in the Spearman correlation added during peer review (r_s = 0.946, p = 3e-7, line 140): Table 2 contains only n = 9 cartons with quantifiable vRNA copies/mL (Carton 33 was negative on re-test), and for n = 9 (or n = 10), r_s = 0.946 yields two-sided p = 1.1e-4 (or 3.5e-5), not 3e-7 (indicating pseudoreplication across 8 segments x 9 cartons or inclusion of negative controls)

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Perform orthogonal protein-level validation (e.g., immunohistochemistry) for candidate diagnostic genes rather than relying solely on transcriptomic datasets.
Examine whether sex-specific DEGs in females are located on the X chromosome.
Tone down claims of 'clear separation' of Progressing Nevi (PN) in PCA (Fig 5C) given substantial overlap and small PN sample size (n=17), and address anatomical site differences.
Specify the batch-effect correction algorithm (ComBat) used when merging the three RNA-seq discovery cohorts.

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe partial batch-phenotype confounding during ComBat batch correction across the three discovery RNA-seq cohorts: all 17 Progressing Nevi (PN) samples originate exclusively from the Bastian FFPE dataset (phs001550), which contains zero Benign Nevi (BN) samples (17 PN + 20 CM), whereas the Badal (51 BN + 27 CM) and Schartl (23 BN + 57 CM) cohorts contain only BN and CM; centering the Bastian [PN+CM] batch to the global mean of [BN+CM] batches algebraically shifts the 17 PN samples toward the BN mean, creating an artificial intermediate cluster in Fig 5C.

Information leakage / optimism bias in reporting in-sample training AUCs (0.930, 0.998, 0.9997) on the exact same combined discovery dataset used for 1,000-iteration bootstrap feature selection, and refitting 23-predictor multivariable linear models de novo inside small external validation cohorts (N=28 in Krueger, N=52 in Scatolini) rather than applying locked training weights.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Limitations of public reference databases (incomplete species representation and unverified taxonomic annotations in NCBI) and their impact on eDNA taxonomic resolution across platforms (Reviewer #2)

Origin and impact of negative control contamination in the 2023 campaign, whether contamination differed between filtration/extraction methods, and implications for excluding Xenopus detections (Reviewer #2)

Exclusion of fish from the main vertebrate comparison and need for ecological site descriptions, study area map, and discussion of species ecological traits and habitat use (Reviewer #2, Reviewer #3, Reviewer #4)

ai_only_critical_catches: Uncontrolled sequencing depth asymmetry between Nanopore and Illumina in the split-pool platform comparison (mean per-sample read depth was 5.65x higher on Nanopore for 12S [273,710 vs. 48,459 reads] and 1.87x higher for 16S [227,434 vs. 121,653 reads], confounding the detection of 7 extra taxa by Nanopore without rarefaction or read-depth normalization).

Equal-volume (10 uL, line 56) rather than equimolar pooling of the 48 tagged PCR products prior to sequencing, which explains the extreme 4-5 order-of-magnitude variance in per-sample read depth (3 to 161,352 reads on Illumina 12S; 18 to 2,424,297 reads on Nanopore 12S).

Internal arithmetic inconsistency on line 111 ('eDNA-based methods yielded 25 detections across all four primary terrestrial vertebrates, out of which 14 were at the species level and 5 at the genus and 7 at the family level', where 14 + 5 + 7 = 26, conflating the 25 Nanopore detections with the 26 combined eDNA detections from 18 shared + 7 Nanopore-only + 1 Illumina-only on line 103) and typographical error on line 74 ('primary non-terrestrial vertebrate classes' instead of 'primary terrestrial vertebrate classes').
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Reviewer #1 wrote one-word evaluations ('Abstract satisfactory / Introduction satisfactory') and asked the authors of an environmental water DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding study to 'add the morphological identification characters of your each identify species and compare it with previous publication', misunderstanding that aqueous eDNA metabarcoding does not capture physical specimens for morphological measurement.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Experimental mass-spectrometry organelle proteomes are incomplete and biased toward abundant proteins in non-model species, so many algorithmically predicted proteins labeled as 'False Positives' may actually be true imported proteins missing from experimental reference catalogs (R2).
Existence of non-canonical / N-terminal targeting sequence (NTS)-independent import pathways means sequence predictors relying on NTS cannot reach 100% sensitivity (R1 Point 2).
Need to evaluate or discuss additional subcellular localization predictors (SUBAcon, cropPAL, ATP, BaCelLo) and expand literature coverage on dual targeting (R2).
Need to include explicit mathematical definitions for sensitivity and precision in Methods and deposit all custom scripts and datasets in a public repository (R3).

ai_only_critical_catches: Circularity and phylogenetic ascertainment bias in the 171-species OrthoFinder benchmark (Figure 3): defining ground-truth organelle proteomes across 171 species solely by sequence orthology to predominantly angiosperm experimental proteomes guarantees that lineage-specific organelle proteins ('pan-proteome') in distant bryophytes and algae are scored as False Positives, mechanically driving the negative correlation with evolutionary distance from Arabidopsis.

Terminological mismatch in Abstract (line 8) and Figure 2 caption (line 45), which claim to evaluate 'specificity' (TN / (TN + FP)) whereas the Methods equations and Figure 2C-D exclusively define and plot Sensitivity and Precision.

Exclusion of TargetP 2.0 'thylakoid' luminal predictions (~100 plastid proteins in Arabidopsis) from the primary plastid benchmark in Figure 2A/C (and mis-citation of Fig 1A instead of Fig 2A in Methods line 149).
Absence of formal regression/correlation test statistics (R^2, slope, p-value) or phylogenetic independent contrasts across the 171 species in Figure 3C.

records.authors: Shibai A, Izutsu M, Kotani H, Furusawa C.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: The non-monotonic downturn in adaptation speed and the exponential fit of ancestral growth rate vs. mutation rate rely entirely on a single extreme outlier double-mutant strain (LQ, delta-mutL delta-dnaQ), whose severe baseline growth defect likely reflects synthetic DNA replication/MMR stress rather than mutation rate alone

Confounding by distinct mutational spectra across DNA repair knockouts (e.g., AT->CG transversions in delta-mutT vs. transitions in MMR mutants) and request for whole-genome sequencing of evolved antibiotic-resistant lineages
Exclusion of insertions and deletions (indels) from baseline mutation rate estimates
Unrealistic model assumption that log-MIC increases linearly and without bound with each mutation (b_i = b_0 + i*epsilon) without diminishing returns or saturation
Speculative and biologically weakly grounded correlation between inferred mutational benefit epsilon and antibiotic molecular weight across only 5 drugs
Misinterpretation of prior literature regarding MMR hyperactivation vs. Pol III processivity in delta-mutL growth defects

ai_only_critical_catches: Deterministic continuous ODE formulation (Eq. 1) allows fractional cells (M_i << 1 cell, OD620 < 1.5e-9) to instantaneously populate multi-mutant compartments at t > 0 and survive 100-fold serial dilutions, failing to capture stochastic waiting times for discrete beneficial mutations or finite-population Muller's ratchet in 2e5-cell bottlenecks

Unreported numerical value and structural non-identifiability of the beneficial mutation fraction parameter alpha (p_b = alpha * p), which is collinear with epsilon and beta in the deterministic ODE trajectory

Pseudoreplication in the Mann-Whitney U-test (p < 0.01) comparing strain LQ (n=4 technical replicates of 1 genotype) against 5 distinct genotypes pooled as n=20 independent observations, and underpowered classification of bacteriostatic (n=2 drugs) vs. bactericidal (n=3 drugs) classes

records.authors: Zhu H, Slonim DK.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Need for an ablation/dropout simulation experiment to prove that Dropout Augmentation (DA) directly addresses zero-inflation by artificially dropping out data points at varying proportions and comparing DAZZLE vs. DeepSEM stability (R1).

Non-stationarity of developmental mouse microglia scRNA-seq data across time points (E14, P4/P5, P30, P100) and lack of quantitative ground-truth TF-target validation (e.g., TRRUST v2 / TFLink) in the microglia case study (R1, R4).
Unclear contribution and lack of ablation for the auxiliary DA noise classifier C_DA on final GRN inference accuracy (R2).

Mathematical formulation and notation defects in Equations 4-9, including what happens when a pre-existing natural zero is masked again by M_DA and improper matrix notation (I - M_DA) in Equation 9 (R1; R1 noted in Round 1 that their mathematical comments were ignored by the authors).
Missing PIDC baseline comparator and missing AUROC metric in the BEELINE single-cell GRN benchmark evaluation (R1, R2, R3).
Lack of concrete wall-clock runtime and parameter count comparisons between DeepSEM and DAZZLE (R4).

ai_only_critical_catches: Inverted fraction in Equation 12 for AUPRC Ratio: the formula multiplies AUPRC by (Positives / Total Instances) instead of dividing by the random-predictor baseline prior, which is a 10^4- to 10^6-fold mathematical inversion.

Autoencoder objective mismatch in Equations 4-7 and hyperparameter symbol contradiction: the decoder likelihood p_theta(X'|Z') and L_recon are written as reconstructing the artificially corrupted matrix X' rather than the uncorrupted matrix X, and the L1 sparsity regularization weight is denoted chi in the text (lines 171, 200) but gamma in Equation 10.

Biological misattribution in the microglia case study (Fig 4b, lines 118-127): non-TF surface receptors, complement subunits, lysosomal enzymes, and iron-storage proteins (C1qc, Hexb, P2ry12, Ftl1, Tmsb4x, Ctsd) are presented as transcriptional regulators of Tmem119 and Apoe because the model does not constrain source nodes to transcription factors.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Clarify the theoretical and algorithmic differences between the proposed GEM algorithm and standard EM, add a notation table and workflow diagram, and compare methods at a unified FDR threshold (Reviewer #1)

Validity of the Gaussian graphical model assumption on zero-inflated/compositional microbiome and gene expression datasets, comparison against Bayesian spike-and-slab and graphical horseshoe priors, and sensitivity/computational cost of tuning hyperparameters alpha and beta (Reviewer #2, Reviewer #3)

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematical mischaracterization of Algorithm 1 as a Generalized EM (GEM) algorithm for marginal posterior maximization: instead of taking expectations over latent variables to maximize the marginal posterior p(Omega | Y), Algorithm 1 maximizes the joint log-posterior log p(Omega, Phi, B | Y) coordinate-wise (Iterative Conditional Modes / block coordinate ascent), which converges to a different mode than marginal EM due to Wishart log-determinant Jacobian differences.

Algebraic simplification of the hyperparameter selection criterion in Equation 28 to F1_hat(gamma) = 2*(E_hat(gamma) - FP_hat(gamma)) / (E_hat(gamma) + p), revealing that setting K = p = 100 acts as a hidden oracle matched to the exact true edge count (p - 1 = 99) of the simulated scale-free spanning trees.

Ambiguous row-wise ('within each sample') permutation specification in Section 2.8 (line 387), which assumes identical marginal distributions across variables and induces negative equicorrelation (-1/(p-1)) rather than preserving variable-specific marginals as column-wise permutation does.

Conditional Wishart variance plug-in in Equation 22, Var_hat(omega_ij) = (nu + n)*(w_ij^2 + w_ii*w_jj), which treats point estimates Phi_hat and B_hat as fixed constants and omits the hierarchical posterior variance component Var_{Phi|Y}(E[omega_ij | Phi, Y]).
concordance.human_anomaly_details: In Round 2 (Decision Letter 1, lines 181-185), Reviewer #1 conditioned final acceptance on adding citations to two unrelated biomedical engineering/ML papers ('The background in introduction can be further strengthened by citing some related studies on advanced computational models and their biomedical applications, such as DOI:10.1038/s41551-024-01312-5, DOI: 10.1109/JBHI.2025.3585290'), prompting the journal editor to insert a formal warning note regarding reviewer citation demands.

records.title: Inferring pathway activity from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data with PaaSc.
records.authors: Liao X, Hong Y, Feng Y, Li H, Fang H, Shi J.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Insufficient methodological and theoretical explanation of how PaaSc selects and weights Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) dimensions and why linear regression on MCA axes outperforms CelliD and GSDensity (R1, R3).
Missing mathematical definition of Spatial Mutual Information (SMI) in the Methods section and unclear interpretation of SMI values in spatial transcriptomics benchmarks (R2).
Inconsistent and arbitrary statistical significance thresholds (p or FDR cutoffs of 0.05, 0.001, and 0.0001) across different figures and analyses (R1).
Overstated claims of 'superior' performance when empirical AUC scores on several cell-type identification benchmarks are nearly indistinguishable from GSDensity and CelliD (R1, R3).

ai_only_critical_catches: Direct mathematical contradiction between Results/Figure 1D and Methods Equation 7: Results (line 36) and Figure 1D explicitly state that MCA dimension weights combine the regression t-value (primary weight) and the proportion of variance explained (secondary weight), whereas Methods Equation 7 defines weights purely from normalized t-statistics without any variance-explained term.

Sign-cancellation and division-by-zero vulnerabilities in column weight normalization w_{ij}^* = w_{ij} / sum_i w_{ij} (Equation 7): because t-statistics from two-sided tests (p < 0.05) can have mixed signs across dimensions or all dimensions can fail to reach p < 0.05 under the null, the denominator sum_i w_{ij} can approach or equal zero.

Unadjusted multiple hypothesis testing across K in [20, 50] MCA dimensions per gene set: filtering dimensions at unadjusted p < 0.05 guarantees 1 to 2.5 false-positive MCA dimensions per random gene set.

Internal dataset count contradictions across text and figures: TISCH tumor immune datasets are reported as 136 in Abstract/Results line 70, 140 in Results line 74/Fig 3A, and 118 in Discussion line 153; bulk RNA-seq senescence datasets are reported as 41 in Results line 90/Methods line 219 but 50 in Fig 4A; and REAP-seq PBMC cell types are stated as nine in Results line 55 while only eight are listed.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Incomplete taxon sampling (only 13 of ~50 valid Bryconidae species included) requires caution in phylogenetic, sister-species (e.g., Salminus affinis vs. S. brasiliensis), and biogeographic interpretations.

Inconsistent and confusing species vs. mitogenome counts across the text and table captions (11 species vs. 13 species vs. 19 mitogenomes, including Table 2 caption originally stating 19 species instead of 13).
Inaccurate taxonomic diversity citations (citing Lima 2004 instead of Lima 2017) and overgeneralization of Magdalena-Cauca basin grouping in the Abstract.

ai_only_critical_catches: Internal table row omissions and duplications in the published Tables 3 and 4: both captions claim to present '19 mitogenomes of 13 Bryconidae species', but both tables contain only 18 rows because Brycon chagrensis 29B07 is silently omitted, and Table 4 merges both B. amazonicus samples into a single row label ('B. amazonicus 58483 /LBP-14082') while duplicating 'B. amazonicus LBP-14082' on the immediately following row.

Strand-orientation sign flip in AT skew for Brycon chagrensis 29B07: Table 2 reports an AT skew of -0.056 (whereas conspecific B. chagrensis 28B05 is +0.055), indicating the RNA-seq mitogenome contig for 29B07 was reverse-complemented on the opposite strand when calculating base composition, and was silently omitted when stating in the text that all AT skews ranged from +0.015 to +0.071.
Contradiction between the Results text (stating mt-rnr1 length ranged from 946 to 992 bp) and Table 3 (where all 18 reported mt-rnr1 lengths lie strictly between 946 and 957 bp).

Unspecified statistical test, silent exclusion of 5 mitogenomes (n=7 vs. n=7 inferred from .29 and .57 decimal means), and intraspecific pseudoreplication (treating multiple individuals of the same species as independent observations) in the regional mitogenome length comparison (p = 0.011).

Partitioning the 13 mitochondrial protein-coding genes only by gene rather than by codon position (1st/2nd vs. 3rd codon positions) in IQ-TREE 2, despite high 3rd-codon-position saturation across deep Characiformes divergences.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Clarify experimental details of the dual-culture confrontation assay (how uniform 6 mm mycelial plugs were cut and how mycelia were separated from cellophane membranes).
Explain the bioinformatics methods used for PCA and secreted protein identification.
Fix typographical and formatting errors (e.g., 'figure 21' typo, moving the experimental setup diagram to S1 Fig, removing 'the' before genus names).
Reviewer 1 requested citing two specific Trichoderma harzianum papers in the Discussion.

ai_only_critical_catches: Uncontrolled chronological colony-age confounding across interaction stages S1, S2, and S3: because slow-growing F. virguliforme was plated 3 days prior to Trichoderma and harvested at successive morphological stages, harvesting self-confrontation controls at a single time point (matching S2) explains why F. virguliforme DEGs reach a counterintuitive minimum at contact stage S2 (799 and 159 DEGs) and peak at S1 and S3.

Contradictory differential expression thresholds across the manuscript: Methods and Fig 3 specify |log2FC| > 1 (FC > 2) and FDR < 0.05, whereas Fig 8 caption specifies FC > 1 and S4 Fig specifies FDR < 0.1.

Remaining strain-name and formatting errors in the published text: strain 'Th19A' is repeatedly misprinted as 'Th9A' five times in the F. virguliforme DEG results (line 140), 'amidohydrolase' is misspelled as 'amidrohydrolase', and stray double/quadruple quotation marks appear in the STAR alignment Methods.
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Reviewer #1 (who answered 'I Don't Know' to whether the statistical analysis was rigorous) explicitly demanded that the authors cite two papers co-authored by the handling Academic Editor (Vivek Sharma): 'Differential Response of Extracellular Proteases of Trichoderma Harzianum Against Fungal Phytopathogens' and 'Elucidation of biocontrol mechanisms of Trichoderma harzianum against different plant fungal pathogens: Universal yet host specific response', while Reviewer #2 (Rhydum Sharma) submitted a superficial grammar/formatting review.

Acknowledge the limitation of using a small sample size of mice (n = 6 per group) to rule out rare breakthrough blood-stage infections (citing Kumar et al. 2016).
Quantify mitochondrial colocalization of GFP-tagged PbHscB in Figure 1B using Pearson's correlation coefficient.
Validate liver-stage parasite invasion and development in vivo or in primary/hepatic cell lines rather than relying solely on non-hepatic HeLa cells.

Inappropriate use of a parametric unpaired t-test on binary count proportions of LC3-positive parasites in Fig 2C (n = 200, 107, 137, and 81 pooled parasites across three experiments) instead of a generalized linear mixed model or replicate-level test.

Omission of the actual numerical Pearson correlation (PCC = 0.44) and Manders overlap (MOC = 0.853, 0.894) values from the published Results text and S1D Fig caption despite the authors stating in the rebuttal letter and Methods that they had calculated and added them.

Copy-paste error in the published Fig 4A caption claiming that only WT and PbHscB-KO schizont sizes were imaged when four parasite lines (including PbMei2-KO and PbHscB-PbMei2-dKO) are plotted and analyzed.

records.authors: Askarova A, Yaa RM, Marzi SJ, Nott A.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Compare H-MAGMA risk gene counts and novel distal loop-linked genes against conventional proximity-based MAGMA.

Explain differences in imputation INFO score thresholds across GWAS cohorts and differences in promoter window definitions between PLAC-seq annotation (2,000 bp) and H-MAGMA (1,500 bp upstream / 500 bp downstream).
Discuss limitations of using pediatric epilepsy surgical resection tissue, European-only GWAS summary statistics, differing GWAS sample sizes, and microglial transcriptional subtype heterogeneity.
Provide genome browser visualizations of representative chromatin loops (e.g., INPP5D, MED12L) and quantify shared versus disease-specific pathways.
Address discrepancies between computational integration frameworks such as sLDSC and H-MAGMA.

ai_only_critical_catches: Mechanistic proof that the manuscript's claim of microglial enrichment for ALS in H-MAGMA (contradicting sLDSC in Fig 1d, which shows zero microglial heritability enrichment for ALS) is an artifact of H-MAGMA combining direct exon/promoter SNPs (124 ALS genes in S4A Fig) with distal loop-linked SNPs (47 ALS genes) and microglia having nearly twice as many called PLAC-seq loops (108,802 vs. 61,895 in oligodendrocytes).

Monte Carlo pseudoreplication in the loop-downsampling analysis (Fig 2b and S4B Fig), where a Kruskal-Wallis / Dunn's test was applied across n = 10 random computational subsamples of the exact same PLAC-seq dataset to report 4- and 5-asterisk p-values (**** / *****).

Severe Linkage Disequilibrium (LD) gene-cluster inflation at the extended MHC locus (6p21: BAG6, NEU1, PRRC2A, PSMB8, PSMB9, TAP1, TAP2, MICB, HSPA1A/B/L, TNF, HLA-DRB1/DRA) and the 17q21.31 MAPT inversion (KANSL1, KANSL1-AS1, ARHGAP27, PLEKHM1), where single LD blocks sharing common SNPs and enhancer loops are counted as 10-15 independent risk genes in downstream GO pathway over-representation tests.

Clarification of whether 'three independent replicates' in Fig 1 meant qPCR technical replicates or independent infection experiments/wells
Missing PCR and Sanger sequencing validation figures for the CRISPR-Cas9 edited PK15 clones
Omission of continuous European wild boar introgression into free-range Iberian pigs as a key explanation for high Hap2 frequency in Iberian pigs

ai_only_critical_catches: Fundamental population-genetic confounding in the domestic pig positive selection test (Tables 2-3): conditioning on homozygosity for a recently derived focal SNP (Cys/Cys, Hap1) within the same 675 bp non-recombining coding region trivially yields near-zero haplotype diversity even under neutrality, while pooling European and Asian breeds in the ancestral Arg/Arg group induces a strong Wahlund effect (G_is = 0.439)

Non-standard manual genotyping of 751 public ENA raw sequencing datasets by aligning reads to a 675 bp transcript via web NCBI BLAST and visually calling genotypes in a multi-sequence alignment viewer without read-depth or base-quality thresholds

Incomplete reporting of PAML CODEML M8 vs M7 parameters (omitting p1, omega_s > 1, and Bayes Empirical Bayes posterior probabilities in Table 4, plus overlapping species counts 22 + 16 + 10 = 48 > 40)

records.authors: Nielsen T, Kervadec A, Theis JL, Missinato MA, Marchant J, Romero M, Marchetti K, Lamba A, Zeng XI, Berenguer M, Walls SM, Schroeder A, Birker K, Duester G, Grossfeld P, Nelson TJ, Olson TM, Ocorr K, Bodmer R, Vogler G, Colas AR.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Need for direct experimental evidence of nucleolar stress beyond p53 activation and clarification of downstream mechanisms
Lack of cell-type specificity of RP knockdown on proliferation (affecting actinin-negative fibroblasts as well as cardiomyocytes)
Failure to show reduced RPS15A transcript expression in family 75H proband cells carrying the c.-95G>A promoter variant (authors admitted no reduction in day 25 CMs in rebuttal)

Weak human genetic evidence in the 25 HLHS trios and family 75H: candidate RP variants (including RPS15A c.-95G>A with MAF = 0.662%, carried by 1 in 76 individuals) are too common and have mild CADD scores incompatible with rare HLHS prevalence without an independent validation cohort
Missing methodological parameters for STRING and PANTHER network enrichment testing

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe expression-quartile ascertainment bias in the STRING/PANTHER enrichment analysis (5.24-fold, p = 0.0028) and lack of a matched control trio cohort: because the WGS filtering pipeline required candidate genes to sit in the upper quartile of embryonic/fetal heart expression, and all 80 ribosomal protein genes are ubiquitously in the top expression quartile, testing the 292 filtered genes against the unstratified whole proteome (instead of an expression-matched background or control trios) artificially inflates RP enrichment

Internal functional contradictions in Table 1: knockdown of RPL13A (201H) and RPL36A had no effect on hPSC-CM proliferation (RPL13A also had no fly phenotype), rps28 CRISPR mutants had no heart phenotype in zebrafish, and knockdown of RPL3L (96H, the muscle-specific RP paralog) actually elevated CM proliferation (opposite to the proposed disease mechanism), plus 3 rows in Table 1 omit the Proband ID

Clinical syndrome mismatch with Diamond-Blackfan Anemia (DBA): heterozygous loss-of-function in core RP genes (including RPS17, RPS15, RPL26, RPS28) causes DBA (bone marrow failure / macrocytic anemia), yet no hematological or DBA clinical evaluation is addressed for the HLHS probands

Inappropriate statistical test reporting in Figure 7 (caption reports Chi-square tests on continuous replicate-level percentage averages of % CDKN1A+ and % EdU+ cells across n=4 biological wells, contradicting the Student's t-test stated in Methods) and unadjusted multiple comparisons across the 80 RP and 292 candidate gene screens

records.authors: Jongkees MJ, Bogers S, de Vries RD, GeurtsvanKessel CH, Miranda Afonso P, Hensley KS, Rijnders BJA, Brinkman K, Rokx C, Roukens AHE.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Potential selection/survival bias from retrospectively enrolling 50% (8/16) of the focal CD4 <200 group (alongside 8 participants with CD4 >=200) one year after primary vaccination.
Ambiguity regarding whether the primary longitudinal outcome model adjusted for booster doses and breakthrough infections, and differences in booster uptake between groups in Table 1.

Unexplained missing data in Table 1 where category counts for vaccines received (n=403) and infection history do not sum to N=448, and unredeemed claim in Methods that comorbidity data were systematically collected.

ai_only_critical_catches: Transposed 95% confidence intervals between the small CD4 <200 group (n=16) and the large CD4 >=200 group (n=432) throughout the Abstract, Results, and S3 Table: the manuscript reports a narrow 95% CI for n=16 (547 BAU/mL, 95% CI 499-595, half-width 48.0) and a 5.2-fold wider 95% CI for n=432 (1399 BAU/mL, 95% CI 1149-1648, half-width 249.5), where the ratio of half-widths (249.5 / 48.0 = 5.20) exactly matches sqrt(432 / 16) = 5.196, proving that the standard errors/CIs of the two groups were swapped during table transcription (and similarly for the slope CIs [-0.320 to -0.311] vs [-0.181 to -0.143]).

Mathematically impossible point estimate and interval in Table 1 for the CD4 <200 group's time since last COVID-19 vaccination ('65 (188-236)' days, where the median/mean point estimate 65 lies entirely outside the interval 188-236).

Inaccurate Table 1 footnote attributing column-percentage sums != 100% to 'Missing data was rounded to one decimal place', when Missing data is reported only as raw counts in footnotes and excluded from percentage denominators.

Unexplained structural specification change between the primary unadjusted mixed-effects model (which includes quadratic time Time^2) and the secondary multivariable mixed-effects model in Table 2 (which omits Time^2 and forces strictly linear time decay across 24 months of multi-wave booster peaks).

records.title: Haplotype function score improves biological interpretation and cross-ancestry polygenic prediction of human complex traits.
records.authors: Song W, Shi Y, Lin GN.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Original submission used a multi-layer neural network with linear activations for PRS integration (which is mathematically equivalent to a linear projection); Reviewer #1 recommended replacing it with regularized linear regression (LASSO)
Explain why LD between adjacent HFS windows is low and quantify the contribution of rare variants vs. 4,096-bp window segmentation
Evaluate robustness of HFS to shifting the 4,096-bp window boundaries (sliding window analysis), reverse-complementing sequences, and two-decimal rounding of Sei predictions

Characterize locus-level HFS vs. SNP GWAS marginal power, quantify false negatives/positives in coding exonic regions, and contextualize limitations of sequence-based DL models (Sei/Enformer) in predicting cross-individual expression variation

Original manuscript selected the best sequence class per locus via SuSiE (causing multiple-testing overfitting); revised to use only the hg38 reference sequence class, and added sensitivity analysis for indels

ai_only_critical_catches: Generative model circularity in the fine-mapping benchmark simulation (Page 2 Lines 40-43): simulated phenotypes were generated directly as a linear combination of the locus HFS scores themselves, guaranteeing by construction that HFS+SuSiE outperforms SNP-based PolyFun.

Asymmetric fine-mapping comparison in real data: HFS+SuSiE was run on individual-level data (n = 350,587) including rare variants down to MAC >= 10 (where 55.3% of HFS causal signals depend on MAF < 0.01 variants), whereas PolyFun and SBayesRC were run on summary statistics restricted to common SNPs.

Violation of OLS regression assumptions in pathway/tissue/cell-type enrichment (Page 2 Lines 11-29): fitting standard Gaussian linear regression to bounded, severely zero-inflated SuSiE PIPs in [0, 1] produces heteroscedastic residuals and anti-conservative t-statistics, forcing the authors to manually discard pathways significant in >50% of traits.

Degrees-of-freedom asymmetry in cross-ancestry PRS tuning (Fig 5C): HFS+LDAK tunes 1,362 parameters (1,361 block-wise HFS scores + 1 LDAK score) via LASSO in the target-ancestry split, whereas the comparator Polypred (LDAK + PolyFun-pred / SBayesRC) tunes only 2 global mixing weights.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Time-scaled phylogeny relies on a fixed external substitution rate from a prior study rather than estimating the evolutionary rate from the dataset itself.
Clarify whether root-to-tip temporal signal regression was performed prior to time-scaling and report 95% HPD intervals for node age estimates.
Claims regarding domestic Polish vs. cross-border Ukrainian HIV acquisition should be hedged given incomplete sampling of the epidemic inside Ukraine.
Recombination and subtype classification relied solely on the partial pol fragment, which cannot detect recombination breakpoints outside pol.
BEAST MCMC chains were run for only 1,000,000 iterations; burn-in fraction and ESS convergence (>200) required justification.

ai_only_critical_catches: Continuous phylogeographic diffusion (Relaxed Random Walk) assigned uniform random spatial coordinates anywhere within large first-level administrative regions (voivodeships), injecting synthetic spatial dispersion noise into inferred viral migration rates.

Internal numerical and denominator inconsistencies across the published text: male count n=1,437 (Abstract) vs. n=1,438 (Results); Ukrainian singleton/dyad percentage 69.5% (Abstract) vs. 69.4% (Results) due to conflating total S&D introductions (682) with Ukrainian sequences in S&D (670); and a unit-of-analysis error referring to 92 dyads as 'sequences' (498 singletons + 92 dyads = 682 sequences, 670 introductions).

Scope mismatch regarding cabotegravir/rilpivirine (CAB/RPV) resistance: the manuscript motivates and concludes with warnings about A6 integrase polymorphism L74I and CAB/RPV failure, but the sequenced fragment (HXB2 2253-3554) covers only protease and partial reverse transcriptase, completely excluding integrase and stripping 43 resistance-associated codons prior to alignment.

records.authors: Lazar-Contes I, Arzate-Mejia RG, Tanwar DK, Steg LC, Uzel K, Feudjio OU, Crespo M, Germain PL, Mansuy IM.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: FACS sorting for THY1/integrin and validation by PLZF (ZBTB16) immunocytochemistry does not isolate pure spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) but captures a heterogeneous mixture of undifferentiated and differentiating spermatogonia plus contaminating testicular somatic cells.

Bulk RNA-seq deconvolution via CIBERSORTx is an indirect approximation that yielded implausibly high SSC purity estimates (99% at PND8, 85% at PND15, 82% in adult) and cannot substitute for single-cell resolution across continuous spermatogonial state transitions.

Imprecise developmental terminology (initially using 'SC' which denotes Sertoli cells rather than 'SPG', conflating fetal/neonatal prospermatogonial stages, and omitting prior ATAC-seq studies on mouse spermatogonia).

ai_only_critical_catches: Systemic experimental protocol confounding between the juvenile (PND8/PND15) and Adult stages across every assay: (a) different FACS surface antibodies used for pups (anti-alpha_v-integrin CD51, clone RMV-7, mislabeled as 'integrin a5' in the Key Resources Table) vs. adults (anti-alpha_6-integrin CD49f, clone GoH3); (b) different RNA-seq library preparation inputs (purified column-extracted heat-fragmented RNA for PND8/PND15 vs. direct lysis of 1,000 intact sorted cells at 85C without RNA extraction for adults); (c) a 5-fold difference in Omni-ATAC cell input (25,000 cells in PND15 vs. 5,000 cells in adults); and (d) different tissue dissociation protocols (trypsin only in pups vs. collagenase IV + trypsin + 30% Percoll gradient in adults).

Misattribution of meiotic/post-meiotic spermatocyte and spermatid contamination in adult FACS sorts as novel intrinsic 'adult SPG up-regulated' biology: the highlighted ciliogenesis/flagellar master regulator Rfx2 and GO terms 'cilium movement', 'sperm flagellum', and 'sperm motility' are canonical pachytene spermatocyte/spermatid markers.
Internal arithmetic error in reported adult DEG counts in the Results ('2483 DEGs between PND15 and adult stage (914 down-regulated and 1579 up-regulated)', where 914 + 1579 = 2493 != 2483).

Unbalanced BAM pooling prior to MACS2 peak calling (merging n=6 PND15 replicates of 25,000 cells each vs. n=5 adult replicates of 5,000 cells each without read downsampling) and omission of the explicit batch factor (B1 vs. B2) from the limma-voom and edgeR design matrices.

records.title: Multi-omics single-cell analysis reveals key regulators of HIV-1 persistence and aberrant host immune responses in early infection.
records.authors: Lee D, Choi SY, Shin SI, An H, Choi BS, Park J.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Small sample size (n = 9 early HIV-1 infection donors), lack of longitudinal tracking or healthy/chronic controls, and need for external validation in independent scRNA-seq cohorts (Reviewer #1, Reviewer #2)
Lack of analysis of non-CD4 immune cell subsets (monocytes, NK cells, CD8+ T cells) and intercellular communication networks (Reviewer #1, Reviewer #3)

Missing scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq quality control metrics (doublet removal, mitochondrial read thresholds), per-donor cell composition breakdown, and unclear Supplementary Table S1 sequencing modality annotations (Reviewer #3)

ai_only_critical_catches: Implausibly high HIV-1 RNA+ call rate in peripheral blood CD4+ T cells (985/4,435 = 22.2%, lines 52 & 93) potentially inflated by relaxing STARsolo minimum alignment length to 25% (--outFilterScoreMinOverLread 0.25, --outFilterMatchNminOverLread 0.25) and nested PCR chimera formation during ONT targeted sequencing without a stated UMI threshold or HIV-negative control benchmark.

Confounding between Th17 cell-type identity and HIV-1 DNA+ integration in Figure 5: comparing the entire Th17 cluster (containing 22 of the 39 HIV-1 DNA+ cells) against all other CD4+ T cells (naive, Treg, Th1, cytotoxic) inevitably identifies canonical Th17 lineage markers (RORC, RORA, STAT3, CCR6) rather than integration-induced chromatin/transcriptomic changes within Th17 cells.

Single-cell pseudoreplication in differential expression and accessibility testing (using cell-level Seurat FindMarkers across 4,435-9,135 cells from n = 8-9 donors without donor-level pseudobulk aggregation or mixed-effects random intercepts).
Internal discrepancy in scATAC-seq CD4+ T cell counts between Figure 5B caption (5,535 uninfected + 39 HIV-1 DNA+ = 5,574 cells) and Figure 5-figure supplement 1A caption (5,608 cells).

records.title: Development of a competition assay to assess the in vitro fitness of dengue virus serotypes using an optimized serotype-specific qRT-PCR.
records.authors: Griffon AF, Rault L, Tanvet C, Simon-Lorière E, Dupont-Rouzeyrol M, Inizan C.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Unreliability of manual fluorescence threshold adjustment to suppress DENV-3 to DENV-2 spectral crosstalk in Figure 3, recommending a quantitative Delta-Ct threshold between matched and cross-reacting channels.
Provide inter-assay precision (%CV), LLOD/LLOQ definitions, sample size justification (N = 96), and justify or replace the Chi-square test with Fisher's exact test.
Validate the competition assay progeny using an infectious virus titration assay (FFU/IFA) in addition to qRT-PCR genome copy quantification.

Clarify that the serotype-specific multiplex RT-qPCR assay cannot distinguish competition between genotypes of the same serotype, and include whole-genome phylogenetic characterization of the tested isolates.

ai_only_critical_catches: Statistically invalid application of Fisher's exact test to continuous qRT-PCR concentrations (copies/uL) and mean percentages across n = 3 biological replicates in Figures 4-7 (ironically introduced during revision after Reviewer #4 asked why the Chi-square test was used instead of Fisher's exact test, with both the reviewer and authors failing to recognize that continuous triplicate concentrations are not discrete 2x2 contingency counts).

Direct internal contradiction in the clinical validation section (line 236), which claims 'Therefore, no false positives were detected' in the exact same paragraph that reports 9 routine-negative clinical samples testing positive for DENV-3 and calculates a DENV-3 specificity of 86.95% (60/69).

Post-adsorption inoculum sampling bias in the competition protocol (line 185): sampling the 'inoculum' from the cell supernatant AFTER 2 hours of incubation on HuH7 cells rather than prior to infection confounds the input mixture ratio with differential viral entry/attachment kinetics, explaining why the measured DENV-1:DENV-2 inoculum RNA proportions (14.8% and 9.9% DENV-1 in Fig 4D) deviate sharply from the 33.6% DENV-1 genome-copy ratio implied by Table 1.

Uncontrolled tissue-composition confounding between multi-flower racemose male buds (containing mature pre-anthesis pollen/anthers) and solitary female buds, and absence of multiple-testing correction across the 18 pairwise tests in Table S7.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Provide runtime and memory consumption benchmarks comparing SpaMI against competing spatial multi-omics integration methods.
Validate SpaMI on additional annotated real spatial multi-omics datasets, including human tissue.
Clarify the semi-supervised prior-guided variant (SpaMI-P) and ensure fair comparison against strictly unsupervised baseline methods.
Hyperparameter sensitivity and generalizability: loss weights [gamma_1, gamma_2, lambda_1, lambda_2, mu], learning rates, epochs, and spatial neighbor counts r were tuned separately for each dataset.
Perform an ablation study on real-world biological data in addition to simulated data.

ai_only_critical_catches: Multiple mathematical and dimensional errors in the Methods equations: asymmetric degree normalization D^{-1/2} A_tilde D^{1/2} instead of symmetric D^{-1/2} A_tilde D^{-1/2} across all GCN layers (lines 171-187); a dimensionally invalid attention fusion formula Z = Z_concat x diag(alpha) that scales concatenated columns rather than computing the weighted sum alpha_1 Z_1 + alpha_2 Z_2 (line 226); and an undefined norm for the n x n cosine similarity difference matrix in L_corr (line 213).

Unvalidated gene-level 'denoising' claims (Figs 3E, 4E, 6D): the autoencoder only reconstructs 50-dimensional PCA/LSI vectors rather than raw count matrices, so projecting smoothed rank-50 representations back to gene space merely acts as a low-rank spatial low-pass filter with no quantitative dropout-recovery benchmark.
Figure 6F caption mislabels the mouse thymus Stereo-CITE-seq protein (ADT) modality as 'ATAC modality data alone'.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Discrepancy between Abstract (-1.98) and original Results text (-2.30) for the Inverse Simpson index regression coefficient, and suggestion to include an additional diversity metric.
Lack of explanation for regression Models 1-5 in Table 2 and inconsistency between raw p-values and BH-adjusted q-values in figure captions.

ai_only_critical_catches: Three-way numerical contradiction in the primary clinical outcome (multivariate virome score association with FEV1 % predicted): the Abstract reports -6.4% (95% CI -10.2, -2.6, p = 0.001), the Results text reports -5.7% (95% CI -9.87, -1.52, p = 0.008), and Table 2 reports -6.1% (Model 1), -5.6% (Model 3), and -3.8% (Model 5).

Direct contradiction between the Results narrative and Table 2 regarding covariate specifications: the text claims Model 3 adjusted for age, male sex, and modulator therapy and that CFRD status was only added in Model 5, whereas Table 2 includes CFRD status and Antibiotics in Model 3 and codes sex as 'Female sex'.

Severe in-sample data leakage and circularity: sPLS discriminant models for CFRD achieved near-random cross-validated AUCs (0.54 for bacteria, 0.61 for phages, with 0 differentially abundant phages at q < 0.2), yet the authors cherry-picked the 'best-performing repetition' and projected the in-sample scores back onto the same patients to predict FEV1.

Uncontrolled confounding by CFTR genotype severity / pancreatic insufficiency (100% pancreatic insufficiency in CFRD and IGT vs 50% in NGT, p < 0.001) and overstatement of a non-significant Pseudomonas aeruginosa trend (p = 0.056, q = 0.449).

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Confounding from cross-sectional study designs (sampling after disease onset or treatment initiation rather than prospectively prior to diagnosis) and variable antibiotic/insulin exposures.
Overinterpretation of statistically non-significant pooled diversity differences (such as in T1DM and asthma) as 'trends'.
Lack of formal statistical validation for the qualitative clustering heatmap comparing disease-associated bacterial taxa against delivery mode and breastfeeding status.

ai_only_critical_catches: Complete omission of quantitative between-study heterogeneity metrics (I^2, Cochran's Q p-value, and tau^2) across every primary and subgroup meta-analysis in the text, tables, and forest plots, violating PRISMA and Cochrane meta-analysis standards.

Severe small-k variance estimation instability in the metafor random-effects models, exemplified by the T1DM pre/at-diagnosis subgroup analysis (k=5 studies, Fig S4) producing an implausibly wide 95% CI of [-2.35, 2.10] (spanning 4.45 standard deviations) while individual study SMDs are tightly clustered near zero (0.01, -0.02, -0.11, -0.10, -0.74).

Direct internal contradiction in age eligibility criteria: Methods states 'We excluded studies where the microbiome was measured at <1 year of age to limit the impact of rapid changes in the infant gut microbiome', whereas the Results, Discussion, and forest plots heavily rely on infant cohorts sampled at <1 year of age (1 month, 3-6 months, and 1-11 months across eczema, food allergy, and asthma studies).

Unreported mathematical conversion of graphical medians and ranges/IQRs into means and standard deviations (citing Hozo et al. 2005 only in the supplement without sensitivity analysis) and pooling multiple arms from the same study (Chua 2018 a/b/c) without accounting for shared control groups or within-study correlation.

Non-systematic cherry-picking of only 4 comparator papers ([115-118]) outside the PRISMA search to construct the 'C-section' and 'no breastfeeding' reference profiles in the ComplexHeatmap clustering analysis, combined with unadjusted binary vote-counting (+1/-1/0) across studies of vastly different sample sizes.

Reviewer #1 consists of 10 generic textbook bullet points—including falsely claiming 'Limiting the included studies to English-only publications may introduce language bias' when the manuscript explicitly stated 'without language restrictions'—and Reviewer #2 consists of 5 paragraphs of generic praise ('This manuscript offers an insightful and timely exploration... It’s clear that a lot of thought and effort went into this work...').

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Lack of benchmarking against spot deconvolution and reference-based single-cell spatial mapping methods (e.g., RCTD, CARD, Redeconve, CytoSPACE, Celloc)

Semi-simulated benchmarks stripped coordinates from ST spots rather than evaluating real cross-platform scRNA-seq + ST pairs (e.g., MERFISH + Visium/Smart-seq) and testing sensitivity across noise levels
Unclear mathematical and biological rationale for the Spatial-Organizing Gene (SOG) index Eq. (13) and its distinction from Spatially Variable Genes (SVGs)
Inconsistent visualization comparing scTour RNA velocity in UMAP embedding space vs. iSORT SpaRNA velocity in physical tissue space

ai_only_critical_catches: Deterministic regression collapse: formulating spatial mapping as a deterministic MLP y = g(z) under MSE loss predicts the conditional expectation E[y|z], collapsing identically expressed cells in non-contiguous or circular structures to their geometric centroid (necessitating an ad hoc manual polar coordinate transformation for the circular human artery sections).

Mathematical circularity (tautology) in the in-silico knockout validation of SOGs (Fig 5a-f): SOGs are defined as the genes with the largest input-output Jacobian gradient ||d_xg f(x)|| of the trained neural network f, and then 'validated' by zeroing out those exact inputs in f(x) and observing a larger MSE shift than zeroing out low-gradient SVGs.

Biological invalidity of applying 'SpaRNA velocity' to adult post-mortem human DLPFC (ID151674) and claiming active cell growth/migration from white matter through Layers 6-2 to Layer 1 (adult cortical neurons are post-mitotic, and embryonic corticogenesis forms Layer 1 earliest before inside-out L6-to-L2 migration).

Complete absence of biological replication in the primary wet-lab human atherosclerosis cohort (n = 1 normal scRNA-seq, n = 1 AS scRNA-seq, n = 1 AS Visium slice), confounding donor identity with disease state.

Clarify whether dominant resistance alleles in cultivar Ouro Vermelho are mapped, mention recessive resistance alleles (co-8, co-Indb), and correct the duration of the biotrophic phase of C. lindemuthianum to ~72 hours

Statistically invalid gene co-expression networks (Fig 6): Pearson correlation networks (r >= 0.9) and Kleinberg hub centrality scores were computed separately within each cultivar across only N = 6 samples (3 timepoints x 2 replicates), where any two genes peaking at the same timepoint trivially achieve r > 0.9.
Methodological misstatement on Line 60 claiming DESeq2 log2 fold-changes (>= 2.0) are 'TPM-based' (DESeq2 computes log2FC from size-factor-normalized negative binomial GLMs on raw counts, not TPMs).

Lack of discussion regarding clinical dose-limiting toxicities of pan-BET (BRD4) inhibitors in oncology trials (R1 Q2).
Raw sequencing data (156 RNA-seq and 32 ATAC-seq datasets) not deposited in NCBI GEO, with the GitHub repository linking only to a private login-walled Illumina BaseSpace account (R1 Q4).

Severe confounding of PCA Cluster 1 vs. Cluster 2 (the basis for the CDKN2A/CDKN2B biomarker claim in Figure 2F-H) by IDH1 mutation status: 3 of the 4 drug-resistant lines in Cluster 2 (lines 301, 372, 412) are IDH1-mutant gliomas (which characteristically exhibit G-CIMP hypermethylation and intact CDKN2A/B) rather than IDH-wildtype glioblastomas.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Lack of clinical validation for the prostate cancer radiotherapy model (with parameters k_M and C_r chosen by 'clinical experience') and small sample size (n = 10) for the head-and-neck cancer validation cohort.
Omission of Normal Tissue Complication Probability (NTCP) and organ-at-risk toxicity constraints when concluding that SBRT is the optimal treatment regimen.
Simplifying assumptions of homogeneous spherical geometry, uniform cell-cycle radiosensitivity (alpha and alpha/beta) in prostate cancer, and omission of anti-tumor immune responses.
Need for parameter sensitivity analysis and Bland-Altman agreement plots for the clinical validation cohort.
Lack of COMSOL simulation files/code and missing explicit numerical definitions for low vs. high vascular density and modified alpha/beta parameters in the Figure 9-11 legends.

ai_only_critical_catches: Fundamental ODE mass-balance error in Eq. (9) and Eq. (14): the dead-cell accumulation equation dN_n/dt = sum(R_c * c) omits a clearance decay sink (-C_r * N_tot), meaning N_tot monotonically accumulates all cells that have ever died and drives unphysical permanent negative volumetric contraction in Eq. (14).

Biophysically invalid linear Oxygen Enhancement Ratio formula in Eq. (21) (OER = -10 * c_ox + 3), which replaces the saturating Alper-Howard-Flanders hyperbolic relationship and assigns OER = 2.0 at normoxic physiological oxygen concentrations (c_ox = 0.1 mol/m^3 ~ 75 mmHg).

Unphysical initial condition placing 100% of tumor cells synchronously in the G1 phase at t = 0 rather than at the steady-state cell-cycle distribution, plus omission of spatial advection/dilution terms in the point-wise cell-cycle ODEs (Eqs. 1-5).

Severe spatial scale mismatch between the simulated 500 um diameter micro-spheroid (~0.065 mm^3) and the 100-400 mm^3 murine and multi-cm^3 human tumors, where reaction-diffusion oxygen gradients do not scale invariantly.

Continuum fallacy in Fig 8 claiming 'all radiotherapy schemes manage to eliminate all tumor cells' based on linear percentage plots approaching 0%, and a 7-order-of-magnitude unit error in Table 1 listing tumor bulk modulus k as 10.40 x 10^7 kPa (104 GPa, the stiffness of steel).

records.authors: Oshima M, Toyama T, Nakade Y, Miyagi S, Ogura H, Nakagawa S, Yuasa T, Koshino A, Horikoshi K, Minami T, Sako K, Tsuge S, Tamai A, Nishioka R, Miyagawa T, Ito K, Kitajima S, Mizushima I, Hara A, Sakai N, Shimizu M, Tokumaru T, Tsubomoto M, Kikuchi M, Kinoshita M, Nakada M, Mita M, Iwata Y, Wada T.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Severely underpowered sample size (N = 7 total; n = 3 vs. n = 4), inability to verify normality for Student's t-tests, and need for non-parametric Mann-Whitney U tests and effect size discussion.
Missing statistical comparisons for baseline characteristics in Table 1, where baseline BMI is significantly imbalanced between arms (p = 0.03).
Need for within-group paired longitudinal statistical comparisons across baseline, Day 5, and Day 9.
Lack of clinical justification for HOMA-IR as primary endpoint over a 4-day window, arbitrary glucose cutoff of 140 mg/dL, gut microbiome analysis, and unmeasured dietary protein intake.

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematical impossibility of achieving a two-sided exact Mann-Whitney U p < 0.05 with n1 = 3 and n2 = 4 (minimum possible two-sided exact p = 2 / C(7,3) = 2/35 = 0.0571 > 0.05), proving that the significant non-parametric p-values added in revision (e.g., p = 0.03) are artifacts of an invalid asymptotic normal approximation without continuity correction.

The headline between-group difference in plasma D-serine (+0.24 vs. -0.32 nmol/mL, p = 0.03) was driven by a significant within-group dietary-washout decrease in the unblinded control group (p = 0.02 after restricting fermented foods) rather than a significant within-group increase in the risperidone group (p > 0.07).
Mislabeling of a per-protocol/complete-case analysis (n = 3 vs. n = 4 after excluding 1 post-randomization dropout from the 8 randomized participants) as an 'intention-to-treat' analysis.

Unit errors in the Abstract and Results reporting urinary D-serine/creatinine and D-alanine/creatinine ratio changes in 'nmol/mL' instead of 'mmol/g Cr', plus baseline HOMA-IR inclusion criterion violation (1.6 +/- 0.6 in controls despite required baseline HOMA-IR >= 1.6).

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Unclear sample sizes, pooling of 4 rat hypothalami into a single snRNA-seq library per group without biological replication, and statistically non-significant testis histology (p = 0.15 across 8 testes from 4 rats).
Absence of female rats, absence of young drug-treated controls, and lack of histological/physiological proof of neuronal 'senescence'/'stress' or lifespan extension in rats.
Arbitrary 'supervised clustering' neuropeptide gene list and unclear definition of pathway score quartiles c1-c4.
Overinterpretation of non-significant endocrine ELISA p-values (p = 0.078, p = 0.096) and speculative human pQTL Mendelian Randomization analyses.

ai_only_critical_catches: Statistical pseudoreplication in cell-level differential expression (FindMarkers with test.use = 'bimod') and Augur cell-type prioritization on N = 1 pooled snRNA-seq library per experimental group, where individual nuclei are treated as independent biological replicates.
Confounding of treatment effects with 10x library batch effects and subsequent over-correction via Harmony integration across unreplicated single-library conditions.

Non-mutually-exclusive single-UMI subsetting (CreateSeuratObject(..., Crh > 0)) that duplicates multi-peptidergic or ambient-RNA-contaminated nuclei across up to 35 neuronal subsets, plus circular correlation in Figure 2E (defining c1/c4 signatures from pathway quartiles and correlating them back against the same pathways in the same cells).

Unadjusted multiple hypothesis testing across 204 traits x 4 exposures (~816 MR tests at unadjusted p < 0.05) and trans-pQTL pleiotropy (relaxed P < 1e-5 cutoff without cis-locus colocalization) in the human Mendelian Randomization analysis.

records.title: Association of long COVID documentation with clinical outcomes among Veterans with diabetes.
records.authors: Wander PL, Lowy E, Korpak A, Beste LA, Boyko EJ.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Questioned the prevalence of U09.9 patients without a documented prior positive SARS-CoV-2 test and potential exposure misclassification (R3 Point 6).
Requested multivariable adjustment for baseline hypertension, dyslipidemia, and baseline kidney function (eGFR) when modeling clinical outcomes including dialysis (R3 Point 7).
Requested converting weight change from pounds to international units (kilograms) across all tables and text (R1).
Questioned how variations in post-index follow-up duration were accounted for in logistic/Poisson models and how the random index date for unexposed controls was validated (R1, R3).

Challenged the unsubstantiated claim that outcomes 'do not appear to be mediated through effects on weight or glycemia' in the absence of formal mediation analysis, and noted confusion between less weight loss vs. weight gain (R1).
Typo in Abstract mortality odds ratio/CI (8.87 instead of 0.87) (R1, R3).
Lack of differentiation between Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes in the VHA cohort (R1).

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematically impossible subcohort count introduced in Results line 58 during revision: the text states 'A total of 75,944 individuals (0.75%) had U09 without a prior positive test for SARS-CoV-2."' even though only 20,438 individuals in the entire cohort had U09.9 documentation.

Direct contradiction between Table 3 and the Discussion/Conclusions: Discussion (lines 185, 193) explicitly claims Long COVID was not significantly associated with mortality among baseline insulin users, whereas Table 3 reports a highly significant lower mortality odds ratio of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.78-0.90, interaction p < 0.001).
Abstract vs. Table 2 IRR percentage mismatch: Abstract line 21 reports '39% more primary care visits per year (IRR 1.36)' whereas an IRR of 1.36 corresponds to 36% (as reported in Results line 79).

Inclusion of 521,812 prevalent baseline insulin users in the Table 2 denominator (n = 1,896,080) for 'Initiated insulin', and failure to adjust for baseline HbA1c or competing risk of death (12-13% cohort mortality).
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Reviewer 2 provided only 7 one-line generic bullet points ('1. Its inclusive of the objective, relevant methods and key findings. 1. The introduction is clearly written and straightforward... This is generally informative and well written manuscript.'), and in Round 1 Reviewers 1 and 3 signed off on the revision without noticing that the authors' new sentence in Results claimed 75,944 U09.9 cases without a positive test (exceeding the 20,438 total U09.9 cases), left Table 3 labeled as 'pounds' with kg values, and omitted baseline eGFR adjustment.
