records.authors: Deslippe AL, Lavoie KL, Bacon SL, Cohen TR, iCare Platform.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Explain the rationale for using p < 0.10 to screen interaction terms and p < 0.01 for final significance.
Clarify how internal consistency of the 4-item COVID-19 infection worry scale was assessed across the three countries.
Conflation of biological sex mechanisms (hormones, stress axis) with social and cultural gender norms when interpreting cross-country behavioral differences.
Clarify selection criteria and potential selection bias in choosing only Canada, Colombia, and Ireland out of the 42 countries in the iCARE study.
Failure to estimate a pooled multi-country model testing country-level interaction terms rather than running separate country-stratified logistic regressions with vastly different sample sizes.

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematical impossibilities and corrupted numbers in published Tables 1 and 3: in Table 3 (Colombia), point estimates fall completely outside their own reported confidence intervals for Infection worry on Healthy eating (OR = 1.45, CI = 0.94-1.40) and Psychological distress x sex on Physical activity (OR = 1.78, CI = 0.95-1.46); Wave 3 Alcohol has a decimal typo in the lower bound (.115 instead of 1.15); Table 1 reports Ireland Female 'Clinical anxiety: No' as 1,101 (17.3%) instead of 71.3% and prints the Canada distress t-statistic as '-.21.6*'.

Internal contradiction created during revision where the authors replaced inter-item correlations with Cronbach's alpha values of .86, .81, and .87 but left the text describing them as 'moderate (<.80) internal consistency'.

Inconsistent confidence interval levels (99% CI in main Table 2-4 captions vs. 95% CI in Supporting Information captions) and p < 0.01 significance asterisks placed on intervals (1.01-1.45 and 1.03-1.67 in Table 3) that correspond to p ~ 0.03 under a 95% CI.

Flawed outcome dichotomization that collapses opposite behavioral changes ('favorable changes' and 'no change') into a single reference category, alongside inverted row labels for Alcohol in Table 1 ('Increase/no change' vs. 'Decrease') that contradict the Methods section.

Misinterpretation of the conditional main effect of Sex in regression models containing an uncentered interaction term (Table 2), inverted odds-ratio prose ('decreased their odds of healthy eating by 39%' for OR = 1.39 of eating less healthily), and consistent misspelling of Colombia as 'Columbia' throughout the manuscript.
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Reviewer #2 submitted a generic, LLM-style outline of vague writing advice ('a) provide clearer transitions... b) ensure consistent terminology...') with minimal technical engagement, and Reviewer #1 submitted a 4-line superficial note with broken spelling ('1In the abstract , you should provide full nme of COVID19... put variables into the quation').

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Inappropriate application of unadjusted pairwise Student's t-tests across 3+ experimental groups (pipelines, sequencing depths, abundance profiles), inflating Type I error; Reviewer 2 required ANOVA with Tukey's post-hoc test or multiple-comparison adjustment (R2).
Missing public repository for the simulation and statistical analysis code (R1, R2, R3).

ai_only_critical_catches: Taxonomic database mismatch artifact masquerading as biological 'False Positives': reads were simulated strictly from 42 NCBI RefSeq/GenBank genomes without contamination, but recovered MAGs were classified with GTDB-Tk v1.3 and compared by species name string against NCBI names. Reclassified taxa (e.g., NCBI Borrelia burgdorferi reclassified in GTDB as Borreliella burgdorferi) were scored simultaneously as 0% recovered False Negatives and high-coverage (up to 1,199x) 'False Positives'.
Misdefinition of Precision (TP / (TP + FP)) as 'Accuracy (%)' in Equation 3 while completely omitting False Negatives (which represent 55% to 75% of the 42 input species in the 42S cohorts).

Mathematically impossible standard deviation for 8K MAG recovery (reported as 42.24 +/- 122.35 MAGs per community across 69 communities totaling 2,915 MAGs) and 100-fold percentage conversion errors in species-pair recovery rates (0.11%, 0.31%, 0.26% reported instead of 11%, 31%, 26%).
Misapplication of the Multi-Metagenome (MM) differential-coverage binning algorithm across simulated libraries where relative species abundances were held identical and only sequencing depth varied.

Internal contradictions in simulated Illumina read length (2 x 150 bp in Design line 206 vs. 125 bp in Processing line 9) and Figure 5 caption falsely attributing taxonomic classification to the assembler IDBA-UD.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Technical batch and platform bias from combining 38 paired-end Illumina MiSeq (2x300 bp) samples with 6 single-end NovaSeq 6000 (1x300 bp) samples.
Small sample size in Group B (n = 10 vs n = 34 in Group A) and unadjusted confounding by antihypertensive/antidiabetic medications, diet, and physical activity.
Need for a baseline demographic/clinical summary table (Table 1) and clarification of Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment.

ai_only_critical_catches: Denominator calculation error in Table 1 (added during revision): for Group B (n = 10), the authors divided medication counts by the total cohort size (N = 44) instead of Group B's sample size (n = 10), reporting 2/44 = 4.5% (true rate 20.0%), 1/44 = 2.2% (true rate 10.0%), and 3/44 = 6.82% (true rate 30.0%), while dividing Group A counts by n = 34, creating a false 10-fold disparity in reported medication rates.

Severe confounding by age at menopause: because Group A (54.74 yr) and Group B (57.30 yr) have nearly identical chronological ages (p = 0.254) while Group B is >=10 years post-menopause, Group B consists almost entirely of women with early/premature menopause (mean age at menopause 43.8 yr vs 50.6 yr in Group A).

Unequal sample-size rarefaction artifact in Table 3: comparing pooled taxon presence across n = 34 samples in Group A versus n = 10 samples in Group B without rarefaction guarantees ~3.4x higher rare-taxon discovery in Group A purely by sampling depth.

Multiple internal inconsistencies: SILVA v132 in Methods vs SILVA v138 in Figures 6-8 captions; Supporting Information captions labeling 'Spearman's correlation... Parametric data'; and sample collection dates stated as 'January 2020 and January 2025' vs 'March 2020 and January 2021'.

Arithmetic and unit errors in Table 1: sawdust Total Carbon (593.2 g/kg) / Total Nitrogen (2.6 g/kg) equals 228.15, but is misreported as 288.2; dimensionless C/N ratios are erroneously labeled with mass-fraction units '(g/kg)'.

Missing HT-qPCR normalization formula (whether 16S rRNA copies or dry-weight mass was used to define 'absolute abundance'), contradictory SparCC co-occurrence network input descriptions on line 97 ('absolute abundance data... at the genus level' vs. 'Relative abundances of the 200 most abundant species'), and discrepancy between 2*E/V and reported 'Average degree' in Table 3.

Misclassification of universal bacterial housekeeping genes as specialized plant-growth-promoting and heavy-metal-resistance traits in Tables 2 and 3: trpC (housekeeping L-tryptophan biosynthesis enzyme) is misclassified as 'Phytohormone synthesis', ppa (inorganic pyrophosphatase), maf (dUTPase/septum formation), and rnhA (RNase H) are misclassified as 'Phosphate solubilization', and ftsH/htpX (membrane quality-control proteases) are misclassified as Zn resistance and antifungal biocatalysts.

Unresolved contradiction between pan-genome methods in Section 2.7/3.9 (Roary pipeline yielding 17,816 gene families and 2,920 core genes) vs. Section 3.10 (OrthoMCL yielding 8,962 orthologous gene clusters and the exact same 2,920 core clusters).

Inapplicable statistical test in Section 2.8 (Duncan's multiple range test, a post-hoc test for >=3 groups, applied to a 2-group plate assay), false claim in Abstract/Discussion that 'metabolites' were tested when only live bacterial streaks were used, and unsubstantiated attribution of anti-P. oryzae activity to Cluster 23 (arylpolyene / lipopeptide 8D1-1) while ignoring the 95%-identical candicidin polyene antifungal cluster (Cluster 4).

Sample size arithmetic error in Table 1 for GERD (GCST90000514): Case = 78,707 + Control = 354,285 equals 432,992 (or 446,148 with QSkin), but 'Total sample size' is misreported as 367,441 (obtained by erroneously adding Control = 354,285 and QSkin = 13,156 while omitting the 73,207 UKB cases).

Typo in Methods/Tables where both recessive and dominant genetic models for TRPV1 rs4790522 were written identically as 'AC/CC' (R6 Point 1).

ai_only_critical_catches: Pervasive data-table corruption across Tables 1, 2, and 3 that escaped all 6 human reviewers and the Academic Editor: (a) Table 2 reports the 47 T2DM patients as 68% female while Table 3 reports the exact same 47 T2DM patients as 48% female (p = 0.064); (b) in Table 1 (TRPV1), combining CC (50% female) and AC (50% female) yields an impossible 19% female in *AC/CC; (c) in Table 2 (TRPV1), combining CC (83% female) and AC (62% female) yields an impossible 30% female in *AC/CC.

Extensive verbatim copy-paste errors across genotype columns in Tables 1 and 2: in both tables, the entire column of means and SDs for *AC/CC and +AA/AC are verbatim duplicates of the Total column; *TT/CT and +CT/CC share identical SDs across every variable; Table 2 reports a BMI SD of +/- 0.0 across 12 individuals (TRPV1 CC: 26.9 +/- 0.0); Table 2 swaps the combined genotype sample sizes for TRPV1 (listing n=35 for AC/CC instead of 12+21=33 and n=33 for AA/AC instead of 21+14=35); and Table 1 prints the sample size '42' inside the p-value column.

Contradictory allele definitions across the manuscript: the TT genotype of TAS1R3 rs307355 is defined as the 'wildtype' in Methods (line 72), Table 1, Table 2, and Figures 3 & 5, but is called the 'homozygous risk allele (TT/AA)' in the Abstract, Results (line 180), and Discussion.

Mathematically inconsistent subgroup counts added in Results line 180: a subgroup of n = 21 cannot have a categorical prevalence of 77.8% (7/9 = 77.8%, 16/21 = 76.2%) and a subgroup of n = 13 cannot have a prevalence of 35.3% (6/17 = 35.3%).

Algebraic operator error in the published risk score equation (Section 2.4, line 71): '+ TNFRSF9 + (-0.0503)' uses an addition sign instead of multiplication.

Internal contradictions in cell and cluster counts: Section 2.1 reports '38,985 genes from 29,733 cells per sample' (which is the pooled total across all 9 samples, not per sample) and '9 major cell clusters' (Fig 1a) versus '12 major cell clusters' (Fig 1c).

Overclaiming tumor microenvironment and immunotherapy stratification when ESTIMATE (ImmuneScore, StromalScore, TumorPurity) and TIDE scores are completely null between high- and low-risk groups (all p > 0.05).

records.title: Digital twin for sex-specific identification of class III antiarrhythmic drugs based on in vitro measurements, computer models, and machine learning tools.
records.authors: Bai J, Wang W, Zhang X, Lu H, Zhang H, Panfilov AV, Zhao J.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: High rejection rate during baseline population calibration (only 11,847 accepted out of 100,000 initial models) and lack of clarity on how 11,847 baseline models expanded into 60,599 drug intervention models.
Strong collinearity between Delta_RMP and Delta_APA (r = -0.88) potentially distorting SHAP feature importance rankings, prompting a request for PCA dimensionality reduction.

Overly simplistic binary classification framing (Class III vs. non-Class III rather than multi-class Vaughan Williams classification or proarrhythmic risk stratification) and limited methodological novelty.

ai_only_critical_catches: Catastrophic data leakage in the ML train/test split: performing a random 70/30 row-wise split across 60,599 simulated (virtual_cell, drug) action potentials generated from only 12 deterministic drug pore-block profiles, so that all 12 drugs and identical baseline virtual cells appear in both training and test sets rather than splitting by drug (leave-one-drug-out).

Direct test-set leakage during hyperparameter tuning: Methods Section 5.6 explicitly states GridSearchCV was used 'to find the combination of hyperparameters that maximizes its AUC on the test data set.'

Mathematically impossible confusion-matrix metrics across Tables 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7 where Accuracy (ACC) is strictly greater than both Sensitivity (SEN) and Specificity (SPE) (e.g., Table 1 Male LR ACC = 0.6553 while SEN = 0.6063 and SPE = 0.6198; Female LR ACC = 0.6707 while SEN = 0.5790 and SPE = 0.6225), forensically proven by F1 = 2*SEN*SPE/(SEN+SPE) to be a Python coding bug that substituted Precision (PPV) into the Specificity (SPE) column across every table.

Exact linear dependence among 3 of the 14 features (Delta_APD_tri = Delta_APD90 - Delta_APD50, Delta_CTD_tri = Delta_CTD90 - Delta_CTD50, Delta_CTA = Delta_CTmax - Delta_CTD), reducing the rank of the 14-feature matrix to 11 so that PCs 12-14 have zero variance and yield identical metrics to 4 decimal places in Table 4, which the authors falsely interpreted as PCA feature reduction improving accuracy.

Copy-pasted irrelevant epidemiological methods in Section 5.8 ('Hazard ratios and corresponding 95% confidence intervals were calculated using conditional logistic regression models') and hallucinated claims in Discussion Section 3.3 asserting that 'in vitro patch-clamp measurements' served as 'the foundational training set for our machine learning models' and that Delta_AREA improved 'classification AUC for drug-induced proarrhythmia by ~2.1%.'

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Low consistency between qRT-PCR and RNA-seq expression patterns across abiotic stress treatments
Lack of functional genetic verification (e.g., VIGS) of candidate ZbbZIP genes
Missing data analysis methods in Materials and Methods and missing justification/citations for 250 mmol/L NaCl concentration and sampling timepoints

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe time-scale, unit, and directional contradictions between Methods and Results: Drought stress is sampled at 0, 3, 9, and 15 days in Methods (line 62), but Results (line 158) states that qPCR expression increased at '9 h' (hours) after drought treatment while stating in the immediately preceding sentence that 'Both expression profiles demonstrated downregulated expression of core genes subjected to drought stress'; similarly, cold stress is sampled at 0, 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours in Methods, but Results (line 142) reports peaks at '12-24 d' and '0-1 d' (days)

Inverted and circular Effective Number of Codons (Nc) optimal codon analysis: partitioning a single transcription factor family (275 genes) by its own top/bottom 10% Nc tails to define 'low-expression' and 'high-expression' groups (despite having empirical RNA-seq FPKM data) and concluding that natural selection favors T-ending optimal codons, which is directly contradicted by Fig 4B showing that CAI, CBI, and Fop correlate positively with C3s and negatively with T3s

Absence of any formal differential expression testing (DESeq2/edgeR, fold-change, or FDR-adjusted p-values) or cross-study batch normalization when comparing arbitrary raw FPKM > 10 gene counts across three independent public BioProjects (PRJNA597398, PRJNA1107841, PRJNA784034)

Multiple internal numerical contradictions: total ZbbZIP denominator shifting from 275 to 276 on line 82 ('63.4% (175/276)'), miscalculated nuclear localization percentage (252/275 = 91.64% reported as '92.63%'), and stating exon counts ranged from '2 to 12' while stating in the next sentence that Subfamily S had 'only one' exon
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Reviewer #2 falsely stated that 'due to the large number of members, the authors did not do some common bioinformatics analyses such as gene structure, physicochemical properties and chromosomal localisation' even though all three analyses (gene structure in S2B Fig, physicochemical properties in S1 Table, and chromosomal localization in Fig 1) were already in the manuscript.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: The study fails to identify any specific genes, enzymes, or metabolic pathway responsible for coronene degradation despite the manuscript's title and framing.
Table 1 lacked N50 and read quality (Q20/Q30) metrics for the Oxford Nanopore sequencing data.
Clarify the meaning of the 'Total length' column (~1,152,142) in Table 2 across the functional annotation tools.
Lack of wet-lab functional validation (e.g., transcriptomics, metabolomics, or knockouts) to link annotated aromatic-degradation genes to coronene catabolism.

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematical unit error in Table 2 (introduced in the authors' revision footnote), which falsely states that 'Total length (~1,152,142) refers to the total sequence length (in base pairs) that was processed by each tool', whereas 1,152,142 is actually the sum of translated protein lengths in amino acid residues (~3.46 Mbp of coding DNA in a 3.97 Mbp bacterial genome).

Severe assembly fragmentation (BUSCO completeness of only 81.7% with 11.6% fragmented and 6.7% missing single-copy orthologs) caused by assembling low-accuracy ONT R9.4.1 / Guppy v5.1.13 reads (where only 2.0% of reads reached Q15 and the authors falsely claimed in their rebuttal that Q20/Q30 scores are 'Illumina-specific and not applicable to ONT') using Miniasm + Medaka without short-read polishing.

Bioinformatic artifact reporting 75 eukaryotic retrotransposons (LINEs and SINEs) in a prokaryotic Halomonas genome due to running RepeatMasker with default eukaryotic repeat libraries, paired with a mismatched Fig 5 caption attributing RepeatMasker categories to MobileOG-DB.

Taxonomic reclassification of Halomonas caseinilytica strain 105 to Halomonas elongata based solely on Kraken2 read-level k-mer matching without computing genome-wide Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI), dDDH, or GTDB-Tk phylogenomics.

Unedited internal draft notes left in the published Results text (line 65: '(maybe repot in Mbp or Kbp)'), a logical contradiction in Table 1 ('Number of contigs' expected '<10' vs. 'Contigs > 50 kbp' expected '>10'), and the false claim that 63.04% GC content indicates evolutionary adaptation to high-temperature environments.

records.authors: Yadav A, Ali R, Devi P, Kumari P, Soni J, Garima, Tarai B, Budhiraja S, Shamim U, Pandey R.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Confounding between viral disease and anatomical specimen type: comparing nasopharyngeal swabs in COVID-19 against whole blood in dengue.
Absence of negative reagent/extraction blank controls and healthy control cohorts in low-biomass metatranscriptomic sequencing.
Missing clinical metadata on prior antibiotic administration and comorbidities, relaxed 30% ARG coverage cutoff, and limitations of Kraken2/Bracken on metatranscriptomic RNA-seq.

ai_only_critical_catches: Severe Table 1 header corruption: the authors pasted the median SpO2 oxygen saturation percentages (97, 95, 80, 91) into the Table 1 column headers as the COVID-19 group sample sizes ('Mild (n = 97)', 'Moderate (n = 95)', 'Severe (n = 80)', 'Mortality (n = 91)', summing to 363), contradicting the true group sizes in the text (128, 33, 24, 60, which themselves sum to 245 instead of 251).

Extreme false-positive taxonomic calls in human dengue blood caused by 8 GB minikraken2_v1_8GB k-mer collisions and un-subtracted kitome: claiming 5,805 active microbial species in human blood, including carp fish herpesvirus (Cyprinid herpesvirus 1), spruce-budworm parasitoid wasp virus (Glypta fumiferanae ichnovirus), soil Streptomyces, Burkholderia pseudomallei, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, plus cloning-vector contaminant TEM-116 in 99% of samples.

Mathematically impossible Procrustes M2 statistics (Section 3.6 and Figure 6): reporting M2 = 4.441e-16 in COVID-19 and M2 = 8.882e-16 in dengue (exact multiples of 64-bit IEEE-754 machine epsilon, 2.2204e-16), which can only occur if an ordination matrix was compared against itself or a trivial linear rescaling of itself.

Compositional closure flaw in the GCPM normalization equation (Section 2.4): dividing each ARG's length-normalized count by the sum of mapped CARD ARGs in that sample forces every sample's total resistome abundance to sum to exactly 1,000,000 GCPM regardless of true resistome or bacterial load.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: European-only GWAS ancestry limiting generalizability and potential residual confounding by unmeasured clinical/lifestyle factors (Reviewer #1, Reviewer #2)
Clarify the significance of the Wald ratio in single-SNP analyses and explain Cochran's Q = 2.945 (P = 0.567) heterogeneity result (Reviewer #2)

ai_only_critical_catches: Algebraic error in computing Higgins' I^2 in Table 3: for KOA -> PDRP (5 SNPs, df = 4, Q = 2.945) and PDRP -> KOA (4 SNPs, df = 3, Q = 2.773), since Q < df, standard Higgins' I^2 = max(0, (Q - df)/Q) is 0% for both, but the authors computed |Q - df|/Q without truncation at zero (|2.945 - 4|/2.945 = 35.82% and |2.773 - 3|/2.773 = 8.19%), reporting false heterogeneity of I^2 = 35.8% and 8.2%.

Inappropriate exponentiation of continuous-trait linear regression coefficients into meaningless 'Odds Ratios' in Table 4 (e.g., reporting OR = 3.846 = exp(1.347) for continuous PDRP expression in the forward analysis, and OR = 297.972 with a 95% CI spanning 56 orders of magnitude [1.80e-26 to 4.92e+30] for 3-SNP MR-Egger), while reporting SE(beta) alongside OR.

Severe weak-instrument and degrees-of-freedom collapse in Reverse MR (3 SNPs, where MR-Egger has df = 1) and Multivariable MR Tables 5-6 (where PDRP, KOA, and alcohol consumption are instrumented by only nSNP = 1 each, precluding multivariable identification).

Internal contradictions in SNP selection thresholds and counts: claiming p <= 5e-8 on line 57 while citing a 'less stringent statistical threshold' on line 90 and F = 29 (~p = 7e-8) on line 104, and stating 'all six instrumental SNPs' in PhenoScanner on line 117 when 5 + 3 = 8 SNPs were used.
Unaccounted UK Biobank sample overlap across KOA (ebi-a-GCST007090), BMI, and smoking GWAS in MVMR, plus complete omission of SNP-level instrument tables (rsIDs, effect alleles, betas, SEs).
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Reviewer #1 demonstrated unfamiliarity with GWAS and Mendelian Randomization by writing: 'The p-value was 5.00E-08. It does not make sense to me. Most of the readers could not find it interesting and problematic to get understand the results. Authors can simply use a regression tool to get more comprehensive and understood results.' Reviewer #2 wrote a 9-line superficial endorsement concluding 'The results of this study will be beneficial for all Health workers in their clinical practice. Hence, this study is recommended for publication.'

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Ambiguity in how subsequent SARS-CoV-2 infections (re-infections or control group cross-over infections) during the 3-year follow-up period were handled.
Need for stratification of cancer incidence by specific anatomical cancer types and by COVID-19 clinical severity.
Unmeasured confounding by COVID-19 vaccination status and pandemic-era disruptions to routine cancer screening and healthcare utilization.
Need for Cox proportional hazards model fit diagnostics (concordance index, Schoenfeld residuals) and explicit definition of 'active patient in the past 12 months'.

ai_only_critical_catches: Pre-procedural diagnostic testing bias (reverse causation / ascertainment bias) in March-November 2020: patients undergoing endoscopies, biopsies, imaging, or surgeries for suspected malignancy were systematically required to take a pre-procedure SARS-CoV-2 test (mostly testing negative) and subsequently received a pathological cancer diagnosis shortly after the 30-day landmark.

Failure to account for the competing risk of death (16.9% 3-year mortality; 84,542 deaths) using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, which explains why the apparent protective association is absent in ages 18-44 and monotonically increases in ages 75-99 (aHR = 0.63).

Direct self-contradiction between Abstract/Discussion ('except in Asians') and Results/Table 4 ('reduction in new cancer diagnoses was similar between white, black, Asian, and Hispanic populations', where Asian aHR = 0.73 matches White aHR = 0.74).

Invalid sample size justification citing an online survey-research margin-of-error calculator ('Creative Research Systems') for population polling to justify n = 3 mice per treatment group (and n = 1 in Group A while contradicting this in Section 2.6 by stating 'three groups, each consisting of 3 mice').

Self-contradictory published revision in Section 3.1 (line 154), where the authors retained the claim '349 vs. 280 viable cells, respectively (P > 0.05)' from crystal violet staining and immediately appended a sentence admitting that crystal violet cannot distinguish live from dead cells.

Unsubstantiated claim of higher liver and spleen metastasis in the subcutaneous cell-sheet group based on single anecdotal H&E images without metastatic incidence tables, lesion counts, or human-specific IHC confirmation.
Internal contradiction in Xylazine anesthetic dosing between Sections 2.6/2.7 (10 mg/kg) and Section 2.6.1 (20 mg/kg).

Mathematically impossible and miscalculated 95% confidence intervals in Table 3 and Table 4: Chronic disease AOR = 1.2 (95% CI: 0.9-1.14) where the point estimate lies outside its own CI; EMR COR = 0.63 (95% CI: 0.53-1.15) where the true CI from the 2x2 counts is 0.53-0.76; Nursing COR = 1.29 (95% CI: 0.86-12.32) where the true CI is 1.00-1.66; Table 4 Family size = 4 vs. >=5 reported as COR = 1.02 and AOR = 0.78 when raw counts yield true COR = 1.65 (95% CI: 1.44-1.88).

Internal sample size and percentage contradictions between text and tables: line 87 reports that '45.7% reported having been infected with SARS-CoV-2 (n=3,291)', whereas 3,291/5,843 is 56.3% (and 43.7% is the uninfected proportion 2,552/5,843); line 74 reports 76.8% had chronic conditions while Table 3 shows 76.8% (4,489) did NOT have chronic disease.
Psychometrically invalid FCS dichotomization cutoff of 17.5 with cited AUC = 0.52 (sensitivity 55.1%, specificity 49.6%), which is indistinguishable from a random coin toss (AUC = 0.50).

Direct contradiction in eligibility criteria: line 31 states hard copies were used to reach HCWs without internet access, whereas line 36 lists 'ability to access the online survey using a smartphone or computer with internet access' as mandatory inclusion criterion (4).

Flawed metabolomics stringency (100 ppm precursor mass tolerance on a high-resolution QTOF-MS and FC > 1, i.e., zero fold-change threshold), yielding implausible plant/fungal secondary metabolite annotations (glucoiberverin, m-trigallic acid, gossypol, semivioxanthin) and an Abstract claiming CDP-ethanolamine, glucoiberverin, and m-trigallic acid belong to Phe/Tyr/Trp biosynthesis while Discussion states the opposite.

Pervasive self-contradictions across the manuscript: flagellation described as peritrichous in Abstract (Line 8) vs monotrichous / single polar in Results, Fig 1 TEM, and Table 1; NaCl tolerance reported as 0-5% (Abstract), 0-4% and inhibited at 8% (Results/Description), and tolerant to 1%, 4%, and 8% NaCl (Supporting Info Line 308); pH range 6.0-10.0 (Abstract) vs 4.0-10.0 (Results/Description); temperature range 10-40 C vs 4-40 C; cell size 0.5 um vs 0.7-0.9 x 2.2-3.0 um

Chemotaxonomic self-contradiction: Line 283 claims the presence of minor fatty acid C19:0 w8c in JDE115 differentiates it from other strains, whereas Table 5 (Line 270) lists C19:0 w8c as ND (Not Detected) in JDE115; plus Abstract claims ubiquinone-9 (Q-9) was detected without any quinone method or result in the text

Improper use of the provisional rank 'Candidatus' (reserved for unculturable prokaryotes under ICNP rules) for a readily culturable isolate solely to withhold the strain from public culture collections for commercial biopesticide development (Line 288)

Table 1 missing all text symbols (+/-) because reactions were encoded solely as background cell colors, plus duplicate rows (l-Arabinose, Glucuronamide) and multiple misspelled Pseudomonas species names

records.title: Mannose and glycine: Metabolites with potentially causal implications in chronic kidney disease pathogenesis.
records.authors: Hu Y, Jiang W.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Inferred metabolite associations with CKD may reflect reverse causation or impaired renal clearance/metabolism of amino acids by the diseased kidney rather than true forward causation.

Multiple completely fabricated/irrelevant literature citations in the initial submission (e.g., a 1972 transaminase paper cited as 2023, C. elegans fat mutants, ferroptosis, and preeclampsia papers cited for CKD metabolomics, plus a dead GWAS URL).

Arbitrary filtering from 46 to 29 metabolites using a one-sided positive beta filter (beta_IVW > 0) and failure to apply multiple-testing correction (FDR/Bonferroni) across the 486 tested metabolites.
Leave-one-out sensitivity plots (Fig S4) show that putative causal estimates for key metabolites (including mannose via rs1260326 in GCKR) are driven by single influential pleiotropic SNPs.
Unclear and statistically underpowered metabolic pathway analysis input criteria and thresholds.

ai_only_critical_catches: Direct self-contradiction introduced in the published text regarding FDR correction: Results (line 91) falsely claims 'we applied false discovery rate (FDR) correction to adjust for multiple comparisons, which further supported the robustness of these seven identified metabolites' while reporting unadjusted nominal p-values up to 0.028, whereas Discussion (line 145) admits FDR was not applied and recommends future studies apply FDR.

Statistically impossible instrumental variable counts and F-statistics in Results (line 80): claiming up to 479 independent SNPs for a single metabolite after stringent linkage disequilibrium clumping (r^2 < 0.01 in 500 kb windows) at P < 1e-5 in N=7,824, and reporting a minimum F-statistic of 17.411 that is mathematically below the P < 1e-5 selection threshold (chi^2 = 19.51).

Repeated misspelling of MetaboAnalyst 5.0 as 'Metaconfict 5.0' and direct contradiction between Results (stating metabolites with P_IVW < 0.05 were analyzed at a pathway cutoff of p < 0.10) and Discussion (stating pathway analysis 'included metabolites with P values > 0.10').

records.title: Causal relationship between COVID-19 and chronic pain: A mendelian randomization study.
records.authors: Fan Y, Liang X.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Lack of multiple hypothesis testing correction across exposure-outcome pairs.
Discordant effect directions between IVW, MR-Egger, and Weighted Median for several reported associations and negligible effect sizes.
Missing R2 and F-statistic equations and unclear SNP exclusion criteria.

ai_only_critical_catches: Fatal chronological and causal impossibility: all 13 UK Biobank pain outcome GWAS datasets (ukb-b-* and ukb-a-477, published 2017-2018) were ascertained years BEFORE SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19 existed (0% exposure prevalence in the outcome cohort), making causal post-COVID pain pathways physically impossible and guaranteeing that any signal reflects horizontal pleiotropy.

Scale/unit miscalculation: UKB binary pain phenotypes were analyzed with BOLT-LMM linear probability models, and the authors exponentiated tiny linear probability slopes (beta ~ 0.001) and misreported them as Odds Ratios (e.g., OR = 1.0011).

Incomplete Bonferroni threshold: the authors divided alpha = 0.05 only by the 4 COVID-19 exposures (0.05 / 4 = 0.0125) while ignoring the 13 pain outcomes (4 x 13 = 52 tests, under which every association in the paper is null).
Algebraically degenerate R2 formula in Methods line 50 where 2 * EAF * (1 - EAF) appears identically in numerator and denominator and cancels out.

Direct contradiction between the Results/Discussion text (claiming no significant heterogeneity except Headache and no MR-PRESSO outliers) and Table 2, which reports significant heterogeneity (p = 0.0277) and a highly significant MR-PRESSO global pleiotropy test (p = 0.002) for Back pain, plus IVW heterogeneity for Knee pain (p = 0.0425).
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Only Reviewer #1 (Yuankai Zhang) provided comments in Round 1 (6 brief bullets); Reviewer #2 provided zero comments in Round 1 and only wrote 'All comments have been addressed' in Round 2.

human_substantive_critiques.issue: High similarity in dataset (GSE63060), analytical workflow, and figure design to previously published Alzheimer's disease cuproptosis papers (Lai et al. 2022, Nie et al. 2023) without citation or comparison.
Missing machine learning methodological details (cross-validation scheme, train/test split sizes, R package versions, hyperparameters, and consensus cluster sample sizes).
Clarify drug candidate selection criteria (DGIdb interaction scores vs. docking scores), justify the -7.0 kcal/mol binding energy cutoff, and acknowledge limitations of rigid-body docking.
Reviewer 4 questioned whether the 5 hub genes were selected by PPI degree rather than machine learning feature importance.

ai_only_critical_catches: Internal sample-size and class-label contradictions in Methods (lines 72-84): line 72 claims consensus clustering was performed on '310 patients with AD' (the sample size of the external brain dataset GSE33000) while reporting cluster sizes of n=90 and n=55 (which sum to the 145 AD patients in GSE63060), and line 84 states only the 145 AD cases (70% n=101 train, 30% n=44 test, with zero healthy controls) were used to train a binary AD-vs-Control classifier.

Direct directional contradiction across modalities: FDX1 and GLS are reported as significantly downregulated in AD blood (GSE63060) and clinical RT-qPCR (Fig 12), but are reported as significantly upregulated across AD peripheral blood immune cells in the scRNA-seq dataset (GSE181279) without acknowledging the sign reversal.

Gene-symbol conflation between two distinct kinases sharing the alias 'PDK1': mitochondrial pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 1 (PDK1, targeted by their qPCR primers and dichloroacetic acid) vs. cytoplasmic 3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 (PDPK1, discussed in their T-cell/NK-cell immunology narrative).

Invalid drug-target pairing and physically impossible AutoDock Vina score: claiming the selective SYK inhibitor Lanraplenib targets mitochondrial ferredoxin FDX1, and reporting a Vina binding affinity of -7.7 kcal/mol for dichloroacetic acid (a 6-heavy-atom fragment whose theoretical maximum Vina score is ~ -3.5 kcal/mol).

Self-contradiction between Results line 299 (stating RT-qPCR validated PDK1, FDX1, and GLS, while MAP2K1 and SOD1 were non-significant) and Discussion line 310 (claiming RT-qPCR confirmed FDX1, PDK1, and MAP2K1).

human_substantive_critiques.issue: Unclear rationale for sample selection and choice of SLAF-seq over other genotyping methods, and need for deeper discussion of conservation/breeding implications and study limitations

ai_only_critical_catches: Mathematical impossibility in SNP count vs SLAF tag count: claiming 5,182,931 population-wide SNPs across only 40,941 polymorphic SLAF tags sequenced at 2 x 50 bp (100 bp per tag), which would require 126.6 SNPs per 100 bp polymorphic tag (and 2.18M-3.02M SNPs across 154K-260K tags per sample in Table 2)

Data duplication and sample omission in Table 1: rows DLC (Line 32) and DLC1 (Line 38) have identical read counts (5,251,972), GC% (43.53%), and Q30% (93.16%), while sample SX (present in Tables 2 and 5) is omitted from Table 1

Fatal population-genetic design flaw in Tables 3-5: pooling two distinct species (Camellia taliensis and Camellia sinensis var. assamica) inside four of the five geographic 'populations' (DL, BS, PE each having n=2 C. taliensis + n=1 C. sinensis var. assamica, vs LC having n=7 C. taliensis + n=1 C. sinensis), which artificially inflates diversity in the 3-tree groups and manufactures the claimed 'genetic erosion' in LC

Mathematical contradiction between reported pairwise F_ST and gene flow N_m (claiming N_m = 0.18 for pair A-C where F_ST = 0.217 implies N_m = 0.902), and contradictory clade assignments for DXS3 in consecutive sentences of Line 98
concordance.human_anomaly_details: Both reviewers wrote generic high-level prose comments (in Decision Letter 1, Reviewer 1 pasted raw AI prompt output addressed to the reviewer: 'However, further revisions are suggested to fully address your original concerns...') and missed the impossible 5.18M SNPs in 40,941 100-bp tags and the duplicate DLC/DLC1 row in Table 1.
